The **2010 NBA draft** was held on June 24, 2010, at [The Theater at Madison Square Garden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Theater_at_Madison_Square_Garden "The Theater at Madison Square Garden") in New York City. The draft, which started at 7:00 pm [Eastern Daylight Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Time_Zone "Eastern Time Zone") (2300 [UTC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coordinated_Universal_Time "Coordinated Universal Time")), was broadcast in the United States on [ESPN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ESPN "ESPN"). In this [draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Draft_(sports) "Draft (sports)"), [National Basketball Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Basketball_Association "National Basketball Association") (NBA) teams took turns selecting amateur U.S. [college basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_basketball "College basketball") players and other eligible players, including international players. This draft set a record with five players being drafted from the same school in the first round. The players were [John Wall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Wall "John Wall") (first), [DeMarcus Cousins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeMarcus_Cousins "DeMarcus Cousins") (fifth), [Patrick Patterson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_Patterson_(basketball) "Patrick Patterson (basketball)") (fourteenth), [Eric Bledsoe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eric_Bledsoe "Eric Bledsoe") (eighteenth), and [Daniel Orton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Orton "Daniel Orton") (twenty-ninth), all from the [University of Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Kentucky "University of Kentucky"). This draft also marked the second time an [NBA D-League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Development_League "NBA Development League") player was drafted, with the first case coming in [2008](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_NBA_draft "2008 NBA draft").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NBA_draft#cite_note-1)

The [Washington Wizards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Wizards "Washington Wizards"), who won the [draft lottery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_draft_lottery "NBA draft lottery") on May 18, 2010, used their [first overall draft pick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_first_overall_NBA_draft_picks "List of first overall NBA draft picks") to draft John Wall from the University of Kentucky. The [Philadelphia 76ers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_76ers "Philadelphia 76ers"), who also beat the odds in the draft lottery to obtain the second pick, selected [Evan Turner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evan_Turner "Evan Turner") from [Ohio State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ohio_State_Buckeyes_men's_basketball "Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball"). The [New Jersey Nets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Jersey_Nets "New Jersey Nets"), who had the worst win–loss record in the [previous season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_NBA_season "2009–10 NBA season"), used the third pick to select [Derrick Favors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derrick_Favors "Derrick Favors") from [Georgia Tech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_Tech_Yellow_Jackets_men's_basketball "Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball").

The 2010 NBA draft was the last draft conducted at Madison Square Garden. The [2011](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_NBA_draft "2011 NBA draft") and [2012 NBA drafts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_NBA_draft "2012 NBA draft") were temporarily moved to [Prudential Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prudential_Center "Prudential Center") in [Newark, New Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newark,_New_Jersey "Newark, New Jersey"), while the [2013 NBA draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_NBA_draft "2013 NBA draft") would be held at the [Barclays Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barclays_Center "Barclays Center") in [Brooklyn, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn,_New_York "Brooklyn, New York") as the Garden underwent renovations during those summers of 2011–2013. After 2014, the draft would continue being hosted by the Nets instead of the Knicks, this time at the Barclays Center, despite the renovations for the Madison Square Garden being done by the 2014 deadline, with the only deviation since that time being in [2020](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_NBA_draft "2020 NBA draft") due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic").

This draft class had no [Rookie of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rookie_of_the_Year_(award) "Rookie of the Year (award)") because [Blake Griffin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blake_Griffin "Blake Griffin"), who was drafted first overall in the [previous year's draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_NBA_Draft "2009 NBA Draft"), missed his first season with an injury, but played in the [2010–2011 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_NBA_season "2010–11 NBA season") and won the award. As of the 2025–26 season, [Paul George](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_George "Paul George") is the only player from this draft that is still active in the league.

## Draft lottery

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010_NBA_draft&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Draft lottery")]

Further information: [NBA draft lottery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_draft_lottery "NBA draft lottery")

The first 14 picks in the draft belonged to teams which had missed the [playoffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NBA_Playoffs "2010 NBA Playoffs"); the order was determined through a lottery. The lottery determined the three teams that would obtain the first three picks on the draft. The remaining first-round picks and the second-round picks were assigned to teams in reverse order of their win–loss record in the [previous season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_NBA_season "2009–10 NBA season"). As it is commonplace in the event of identical win–loss records, the NBA performed a random drawing to break the ties on April 16, 2010.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NBA_draft#cite_note-draftorder-72)

The lottery was held on May 18, 2010, in [Secaucus, New Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secaucus,_New_Jersey "Secaucus, New Jersey").[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NBA_draft#cite_note-draftorder-72) The [Washington Wizards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Wizards "Washington Wizards") and [Philadelphia 76ers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_76ers "Philadelphia 76ers") beat the statistical odds by winning the first and second overall picks respectively. The [New Jersey Nets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Jersey_Nets "New Jersey Nets") won the third overall pick.

The basic eligibility rules for the draft are:

The basic requirement for automatic eligibility for a U.S. player is the completion of his college eligibility.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NBA_draft#cite_note-CBA_US-75) Players who meet the CBA definition of "international players" are automatically eligible if their 22nd birthday falls during or before the calendar year of the draft (i.e., born on or before December 31, 1988).[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NBA_draft#cite_note-CBA_International_Age-76) U.S. players who were at least one year removed from their high school graduation and have played professionally with a team outside the NBA (either top-level basketball in another country, or minor-league basketball in North America) were also automatically eligible. Former high school player [Latavious Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latavious_Williams "Latavious Williams") meets these criteria, having graduated high school in 2009, skipped [college basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_basketball "College basketball") and then played professional basketball in [NBA D-League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Development_League "NBA Development League").[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NBA_draft#cite_note-77)

A player who is not automatically eligible must declare his eligibility for the draft by notifying the NBA offices in writing no later than 60 days before the draft.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NBA_draft#cite_note-CBA_US_Early_Entry-78)[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NBA_draft#cite_note-CBA_International_Early_Entry-79) For the 2010 draft, this date fell on April 25. The **2010 NBA draft** was held on June 24, 2010, at [The Theater at Madison Square Garden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Theater_at_Madison_Square_Garden "The Theater at Madison Square Garden") in New York City. The draft, which started at 7:00 pm [Eastern Daylight Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Time_Zone "Eastern Time Zone") (2300 [UTC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coordinated_Universal_Time "Coordinated Universal Time")), was broadcast in the United States on [ESPN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ESPN "ESPN"). In this [draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Draft_(sports) "Draft (sports)"), [National Basketball Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Basketball_Association "National Basketball Association") (NBA) teams took turns selecting amateur U.S. [college basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_basketball "College basketball") players and other eligible players, including international players. This draft set a record with five players being drafted from the same school in the first round. The players were [John Wall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Wall "John Wall") (first), [DeMarcus Cousins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeMarcus_Cousins "DeMarcus Cousins") (fifth), [Patrick Patterson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_Patterson_(basketball) "Patrick Patterson (basketball)") (fourteenth), [Eric Bledsoe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eric_Bledsoe "Eric Bledsoe") (eighteenth), and [Daniel Orton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Orton "Daniel Orton") (twenty-ninth), all from the [University of Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Kentucky "University of Kentucky"). This draft also marked the second time an [NBA D-League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Development_League "NBA Development League") player was drafted, with the first case coming in [2008](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_NBA_draft "2008 NBA draft").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NBA_draft#cite_note-1)

The [Washington Wizards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Wizards "Washington Wizards"), who won the [draft lottery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_draft_lottery "NBA draft lottery") on May 18, 2010, used their [first overall draft pick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_first_overall_NBA_draft_picks "List of first overall NBA draft picks") to draft John Wall from the University of Kentucky. The [Philadelphia 76ers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_76ers "Philadelphia 76ers"), who also beat the odds in the draft lottery to obtain the second pick, selected [Evan Turner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evan_Turner "Evan Turner") from [Ohio State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ohio_State_Buckeyes_men's_basketball "Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball"). The [New Jersey Nets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Jersey_Nets "New Jersey Nets"), who had the worst win–loss record in the [previous season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_NBA_season "2009–10 NBA season"), used the third pick to select [Derrick Favors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derrick_Favors "Derrick Favors") from [Georgia Tech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_Tech_Yellow_Jackets_men's_basketball "Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball").

The 2010 NBA draft was the last draft conducted at Madison Square Garden. The [2011](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_NBA_draft "2011 NBA draft") and [2012 NBA drafts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_NBA_draft "2012 NBA draft") were temporarily moved to [Prudential Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prudential_Center "Prudential Center") in [Newark, New Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newark,_New_Jersey "Newark, New Jersey"), while the [2013 NBA draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_NBA_draft "2013 NBA draft") would be held at the [Barclays Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barclays_Center "Barclays Center") in [Brooklyn, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn,_New_York "Brooklyn, New York") as the Garden underwent renovations during those summers of 2011–2013. After 2014, the draft would continue being hosted by the Nets instead of the Knicks, this time at the Barclays Center, despite the renovations for the Madison Square Garden being done by the 2014 deadline, with the only deviation since that time being in [2020](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_NBA_draft "2020 NBA draft") due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic").

This draft class had no [Rookie of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rookie_of_the_Year_(award) "Rookie of the Year (award)") because [Blake Griffin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blake_Griffin "Blake Griffin"), who was drafted first overall in the [previous year's draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_NBA_Draft "2009 NBA Draft"), missed his first season with an injury, but played in the [2010–2011 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_NBA_season "2010–11 NBA season") and won the award. As of the 2025–26 season, [Paul George](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_George "Paul George") is the only player from this draft that is still active in the league.

## Draft lottery

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010_NBA_draft&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Draft lottery")]

Further information: [NBA draft lottery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_draft_lottery "NBA draft lottery")

The first 14 picks in the draft belonged to teams which had missed the [playoffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NBA_Playoffs "2010 NBA Playoffs"); the order was determined through a lottery. The lottery determined the three teams that would obtain the first three picks on the draft. The remaining first-round picks and the second-round picks were assigned to teams in reverse order of their win–loss record in the [previous season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_NBA_season "2009–10 NBA season"). As it is commonplace in the event of identical win–loss records, the NBA performed a random drawing to break the ties on April 16, 2010.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NBA_draft#cite_note-draftorder-72)

The **2010 NBA draft** was held on June 24, 2010, at [The Theater at Madison Square Garden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Theater_at_Madison_Square_Garden "The Theater at Madison Square Garden") in New York City. The draft, which started at 7:00 pm [Eastern Daylight Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Time_Zone "Eastern Time Zone") (2300 [UTC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coordinated_Universal_Time "Coordinated Universal Time")), was broadcast in the United States on [ESPN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ESPN "ESPN"). In this [draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Draft_(sports) "Draft (sports)"), [National Basketball Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Basketball_Association "National Basketball Association") (NBA) teams took turns selecting amateur U.S. [college basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_basketball "College basketball") players and other eligible players, including international players. This draft set a record with five players being drafted from the same school in the first round. The players were [John Wall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Wall "John Wall") (first), [DeMarcus Cousins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeMarcus_Cousins "DeMarcus Cousins") (fifth), [Patrick Patterson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_Patterson_(basketball) "Patrick Patterson (basketball)") (fourteenth), [Eric Bledsoe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eric_Bledsoe "Eric Bledsoe") (eighteenth), and [Daniel Orton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Orton "Daniel Orton") (twenty-ninth), all from the [University of Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Kentucky "University of Kentucky"). This draft also marked the second time an [NBA D-League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Development_League "NBA Development League") player was drafted, with the first case coming in [2008](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_NBA_draft "2008 NBA draft").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010_NBA_draft&printable=yes#cite_note-1)

The [Washington Wizards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Wizards "Washington Wizards"), who won the [draft lottery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_draft_lottery "NBA draft lottery") on May 18, 2010, used their [first overall draft pick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_first_overall_NBA_draft_picks "List of first overall NBA draft picks") to draft John Wall from the University of Kentucky. The [Philadelphia 76ers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_76ers "Philadelphia 76ers"), who also beat the odds in the draft lottery to obtain the second pick, selected [Evan Turner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evan_Turner "Evan Turner") from [Ohio State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ohio_State_Buckeyes_men's_basketball "Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball"). The [New Jersey Nets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Jersey_Nets "New Jersey Nets"), who had the worst win–loss record in the [previous season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_NBA_season "2009–10 NBA season"), used the third pick to select [Derrick Favors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derrick_Favors "Derrick Favors") from [Georgia Tech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_Tech_Yellow_Jackets_men's_basketball "Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball").

The 2010 NBA draft was the last draft conducted at Madison Square Garden. The [2011](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_NBA_draft "2011 NBA draft") and [2012 NBA drafts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_NBA_draft "2012 NBA draft") were temporarily moved to [Prudential Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prudential_Center "Prudential Center") in [Newark, New Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newark,_New_Jersey "Newark, New Jersey"), while the [2013 NBA draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_NBA_draft "2013 NBA draft") would be held at the [Barclays Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barclays_Center "Barclays Center") in [Brooklyn, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn,_New_York "Brooklyn, New York") as the Garden underwent renovations during those summers of 2011–2013. After 2014, the draft would continue being hosted by the Nets instead of the Knicks, this time at the Barclays Center, despite the renovations for the Madison Square Garden being done by the 2014 deadline, with the only deviation since that time being in [2020](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_NBA_draft "2020 NBA draft") due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic").

This draft class had no [Rookie of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rookie_of_the_Year_(award) "Rookie of the Year (award)") because [Blake Griffin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blake_Griffin "Blake Griffin"), who was drafted first overall in the [previous year's draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_NBA_Draft "2009 NBA Draft"), missed his first season with an injury, but played in the [2010–2011 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_NBA_season "2010–11 NBA season") and won the award. As of the 2025–26 season, [Paul George](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_George "Paul George") is the only player from this draft that is still active in the league.

## Draft lottery

Further information: [NBA draft lottery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_draft_lottery "NBA draft lottery")

The first 14 picks in the draft belonged to teams which had missed the [playoffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NBA_Playoffs "2010 NBA Playoffs"); the order was determined through a lottery. The lottery determined the three teams that would obtain the first three picks on the draft. The remaining first-round picks and the second-round picks were assigned to teams in reverse order of their win–loss record in the [previous season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_NBA_season "2009–10 NBA season"). As it is commonplace in the event of identical win–loss records, the NBA performed a random drawing to break the ties on April 16, 2010.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010_NBA_draft&printable=yes#cite_note-draftorder-72)

The lottery was held on May 18, 2010, in [Secaucus, New Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secaucus,_New_Jersey "Secaucus, New Jersey").[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010_NBA_draft&printable=yes#cite_note-draftorder-72) The [Washington Wizards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Wizards "Washington Wizards") and [Philadelphia 76ers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_76ers "Philadelphia 76ers") beat the statistical odds by winning the first and second overall picks respectively. The [New Jersey Nets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Jersey_Nets "New Jersey Nets") won the third overall pick.

The **2010 NBA draft** was held on June 24, 2010, at [The Theater at Madison Square Garden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Theater_at_Madison_Square_Garden "The Theater at Madison Square Garden") in New York City. The draft, which started at 7:00 pm [Eastern Daylight Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Time_Zone "Eastern Time Zone") (2300 [UTC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coordinated_Universal_Time "Coordinated Universal Time")), was broadcast in the United States on [ESPN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ESPN "ESPN"). In this [draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Draft_(sports) "Draft (sports)"), [National Basketball Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Basketball_Association "National Basketball Association") (NBA) teams took turns selecting amateur U.S. [college basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_basketball "College basketball") players and other eligible players, including international players. This draft set a record with five players being drafted from the same school in the first round. The players were [John Wall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Wall "John Wall") (first), [DeMarcus Cousins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeMarcus_Cousins "DeMarcus Cousins") (fifth), [Patrick Patterson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_Patterson_(basketball) "Patrick Patterson (basketball)") (fourteenth), [Eric Bledsoe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eric_Bledsoe "Eric Bledsoe") (eighteenth), and [Daniel Orton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Orton "Daniel Orton") (twenty-ninth), all from the [University of Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Kentucky "University of Kentucky"). This draft also marked the second time an [NBA D-League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Development_League "NBA Development League") player was drafted, with the first case coming in [2008](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_NBA_draft "2008 NBA draft").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010_NBA_draft&printable=yes#cite_note-1)

The [Washington Wizards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Wizards "Washington Wizards"), who won the [draft lottery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_draft_lottery "NBA draft lottery") on May 18, 2010, used their [first overall draft pick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_first_overall_NBA_draft_picks "List of first overall NBA draft picks") to draft John Wall from the University of Kentucky. The [Philadelphia 76ers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_76ers "Philadelphia 76ers"), who also beat the odds in the draft lottery to obtain the second pick, selected [Evan Turner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evan_Turner "Evan Turner") from [Ohio State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ohio_State_Buckeyes_men's_basketball "Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball"). The [New Jersey Nets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Jersey_Nets "New Jersey Nets"), who had the worst win–loss record in the [previous season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_NBA_season "2009–10 NBA season"), used the third pick to select [Derrick Favors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derrick_Favors "Derrick Favors") from [Georgia Tech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_Tech_Yellow_Jackets_men's_basketball "Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball").

The 2010 NBA draft was the last draft conducted at Madison Square Garden. The [2011](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_NBA_draft "2011 NBA draft") and [2012 NBA drafts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_NBA_draft "2012 NBA draft") were temporarily moved to [Prudential Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prudential_Center "Prudential Center") in [Newark, New Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newark,_New_Jersey "Newark, New Jersey"), while the [2013 NBA draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_NBA_draft "2013 NBA draft") would be held at the [Barclays Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barclays_Center "Barclays Center") in [Brooklyn, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn,_New_York "Brooklyn, New York") as the Garden underwent renovations during those summers of 2011–2013. After 2014, the draft would continue being hosted by the Nets instead of the Knicks, this time at the Barclays Center, despite the renovations for the Madison Square Garden being done by the 2014 deadline, with the only deviation since that time being in [2020](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_NBA_draft "2020 NBA draft") due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic").

This draft class had no [Rookie of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rookie_of_the_Year_(award) "Rookie of the Year (award)") because [Blake Griffin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blake_Griffin "Blake Griffin"), who was drafted first overall in the [previous year's draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_NBA_Draft "2009 NBA Draft"), missed his first season with an injury, but played in the [2010–2011 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_NBA_season "2010–11 NBA season") and won the award. As of the 2025–26 season, [Paul George](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_George "Paul George") is the only player from this draft that is still active in the league.

The **2010 [NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament")** involved 65 teams playing in a [single-elimination tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single-elimination_tournament "Single-elimination tournament") that determined the [National Collegiate Athletic Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Collegiate_Athletic_Association "National Collegiate Athletic Association") (NCAA) [Division I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NCAA_Division_I "NCAA Division I") men's [basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_basketball "College basketball") national champion for the [2009–10 basketball season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_season "2009–10 NCAA Division I men's basketball season"). The 72nd annual edition of the tournament began on March 16, 2010, and concluded with the [championship game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Division_I_Basketball_Championship_Game "2010 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship Game") on April 5, at [Lucas Oil Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucas_Oil_Stadium "Lucas Oil Stadium") in [Indianapolis, Indiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indianapolis "Indianapolis").

The Final Four consisted of [Duke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Duke_Blue_Devils_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team"), making their first appearance since [2004](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "2004 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament"), [West Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_West_Virginia_Mountaineers_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball team"), who were making their second appearance and first since [1959](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1959_NCAA_University_Division_basketball_tournament "1959 NCAA University Division basketball tournament"), [Butler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Butler_Bulldogs_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Butler Bulldogs men's basketball team"), considered the host school and making their first ever appearance, and [Michigan State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Michigan_State_Spartans_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team"), the national runner-up from [2009](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "2009 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament") appearing in the Final Four for the sixth time under head coach [Tom Izzo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Izzo "Tom Izzo").

When Duke and Butler played each other in the tournament final, it was the first title game between private universities in 25 years ([Villanova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1984%E2%80%9385_Villanova_Wildcats_men's_basketball_team "1984–85 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team") and [Georgetown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1984%E2%80%9385_Georgetown_Hoyas_men's_basketball_team "1984–85 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team") met in [1985](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1985_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "1985 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament")), and the fifth such match-up in history ([1942](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1942_NCAA_basketball_tournament "1942 NCAA basketball tournament"), [1954](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1954_NCAA_basketball_tournament "1954 NCAA basketball tournament"), and [1955](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1955_NCAA_basketball_tournament "1955 NCAA basketball tournament") having been the other years). Duke defeated Butler 61–59 in the championship game as [Gordon Hayward](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gordon_Hayward "Gordon Hayward")'s last second desperation shot clanged off the rim. It was Duke's first national championship since [2001](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "2001 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament") and fourth overall.

Entering the tournament, the top four seeds were [Kansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Kansas_Jayhawks_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team"), Duke, [Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Kentucky_Wildcats_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team"), and [Syracuse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Syracuse_Orange_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Syracuse Orange men's basketball team"). Kansas entered the Tournament as the overall No. 1 seed but was defeated in the opening weekend by [Northern Iowa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Northern_Iowa_Panthers_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Northern Iowa Panthers men's basketball team"), the No. 9 seed in the Midwest region. Northern Iowa was one of four teams seeded lower than No. 8 to advance to the Sweet Sixteen, joining the East Region's No. 11 seed [Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Washington_Huskies_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Washington Huskies men's basketball team"), No. 12 seed [Cornell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Cornell_Big_Red_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Cornell Big Red men's basketball team") and the South Region's No. 10 seed [Saint Mary's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Saint_Mary's_Gaels_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Saint Mary's Gaels men's basketball team").

For the first time since [2006](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "2006 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament"), a No. 14 seed advanced out of the first round as [Ohio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ohio_Bobcats_men's_basketball "Ohio Bobcats men's basketball") defeated [Georgetown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgetown_Hoyas_men's_basketball "Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball"). The No. 13 seed in the West Region, [Murray State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murray_State_Racers_men's_basketball "Murray State Racers men's basketball"), defeated No. 4-seeded [Vanderbilt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanderbilt_Commodores_men's_basketball "Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball"), marking the second consecutive appearance for the Commodores where they lost as a No. 4 seed. Murray State very nearly upset Butler in their next game, losing by two points.

One of the more exciting games of the tournament was played at the West Regional in [Salt Lake City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salt_Lake_City "Salt Lake City"), as No. 6 [Xavier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xavier_Musketeers_men's_basketball "Xavier Musketeers men's basketball") took No. 2 [Kansas State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_State_Wildcats_men's_basketball "Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball") to two overtimes before falling 101–96. [Jordan Crawford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan_Crawford "Jordan Crawford") hit a three-pointer with seconds remaining in the first overtime period to force a second.

## Tournament procedure

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010_NCAA_Division_I_men%27s_basketball_tournament&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Tournament procedure")]

Further information: [NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship §Format history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NCAA_Men's_Division_I_Basketball_Championship#Format_history "NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship")

A total of 65 teams were selected for the tournament. Thirty one of the teams earned automatic bids by winning their [conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_NCAA_conferences "List of NCAA conferences") tournaments. The automatic bid of the [Ivy League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivy_League "Ivy League"), which at the time did not conduct a postseason tournament, went to [Cornell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Cornell_Big_Red_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Cornell Big Red men's basketball team"), its regular season champion. The remaining 34 teams were granted at-large bids, which were extended by the NCAA Selection Committee.

Two teams played an opening-round game, popularly called the play-in game; the winner of that game advanced to the main draw of the tournament and played a top seed in one of the regionals. The 2010 game was played on March 16 at [University of Dayton Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Dayton_Arena "University of Dayton Arena") in [Dayton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dayton,_Ohio "Dayton, Ohio"), Ohio, as it has been since its inception in [2001](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "2001 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament").

All 64 teams were seeded 1 to 16 within their regions; the winner of the play-in game automatically received a 16 seed. The [Selection Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NCAA_basketball_tournament_selection_process "NCAA basketball tournament selection process") seeded the entire field from 1 to 65. [UCLA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UCLA_Bruins "UCLA Bruins") athletic director [Dan Guerrero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Guerrero "Dan Guerrero") took over as chair of the Division I Men's Basketball Committee.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-1)

Defending champion [North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_North_Carolina_Tar_Heels_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team") did not qualify for the Tournament, while two schools made their first post-season appearance: [Southern Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Conference "Southern Conference") champion [Wofford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Wofford_Terriers_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Wofford Terriers men's basketball team") and [SWAC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southwestern_Athletic_Conference "Southwestern Athletic Conference") champion [Arkansas-Pine Bluff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arkansas%E2%80%93Pine_Bluff_Golden_Lions_men's_basketball "Arkansas–Pine Bluff Golden Lions men's basketball"). [Conference USA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conference_USA "Conference USA") champion [Houston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Houston_Cougars_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Houston Cougars men's basketball team") made its first NCAA Tournament appearance in 18 years.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-2)

## Game summaries

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010_NCAA_Division_I_men%27s_basketball_tournament&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Game summaries")]

### Midwest Region

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010_NCAA_Division_I_men%27s_basketball_tournament&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Midwest Region")]

#### First round

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010_NCAA_Division_I_men%27s_basketball_tournament&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: First round")]

The biggest upset of the first day came in [Providence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Providence,_Rhode_Island "Providence, Rhode Island"), Rhode Island, where 14th-seeded [Ohio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Ohio_Bobcats_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Ohio Bobcats men's basketball team") defeated third-seeded [Georgetown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Georgetown_Hoyas_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team") in convincing fashion, 97–83, for their first Tournament win since [1983](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1983_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "1983 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament"), when they ousted [Illinois State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois_State_Redbirds_men's_basketball "Illinois State Redbirds men's basketball") in the first round of that Tournament. [Armon Bassett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armon_Bassett "Armon Bassett") scored 32 points for the Bobcats, who shot 57 percent from the field and made 13 of 23 3-pointers.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-6) They advanced to face [Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Tennessee_Volunteers_basketball_team "2009–10 Tennessee Volunteers basketball team"), the sixth seed in the region. The Volunteers held off 11th seed [San Diego State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_San_Diego_State_Aztecs_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 San Diego State Aztecs men's basketball team"), 62–59, on head coach [Bruce Pearl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruce_Pearl "Bruce Pearl")'s 50th birthday. [J. P. Prince](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J._P._Prince "J. P. Prince") and Melvin Goins scored 15 points each for Tennessee.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-7)

In [Oklahoma City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oklahoma_City "Oklahoma City"), [Ali Farokhmanesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ali_Farokhmanesh "Ali Farokhmanesh") drilled a three-pointer with 4.9 seconds remaining to lift ninth-seeded [Northern Iowa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Northern_Iowa_Panthers_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Northern Iowa Panthers men's basketball team") over [UNLV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_UNLV_Runnin'_Rebels_basketball_team "2009–10 UNLV Runnin' Rebels basketball team"). It was the Panthers first Tournament win since [1990](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "1990 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-8) UNI advanced to face top-seeded [Kansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Kansas_Jayhawks_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team"). The top seed withheld an effort by [Lehigh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lehigh_Mountain_Hawks_men's_basketball "Lehigh Mountain Hawks men's basketball"), trailing the 16th seed early in the game and leading by just six at halftime before pulling away midway in the second half for a 90–74 win.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-9)

On the second day of play, 10th-seeded [Georgia Tech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Georgia_Tech_Yellow_Jackets_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball team") failed to make a single field goal in the final 8:19 of play, but sank 13 free throws to hold off No. 7 [Oklahoma State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Oklahoma_State_Cowboys_basketball_team "2009–10 Oklahoma State Cowboys basketball team"), 64–59, in [Milwaukee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milwaukee "Milwaukee"). [Gani Lawal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gani_Lawal "Gani Lawal") led Georgia Tech with 14 points.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-10) The Yellow Jackets advanced to play [Ohio State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Ohio_State_Buckeyes_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball team"), who defeated [UC Santa Barbara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_UC_Santa_Barbara_Gauchos_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 UC Santa Barbara Gauchos men's basketball team") 68–51. Buckeye star [Evan Turner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evan_Turner "Evan Turner") struggled from the field, shooting 2–13 and scoring nine points, and the Gauchos put up a fight, playing from behind most of the game.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-11)

Rounding out the Midwest bracket were [Maryland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Maryland_Terrapins_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Maryland Terrapins men's basketball team") and [Michigan State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Michigan_State_Spartans_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team") in [Spokane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spokane,_Washington "Spokane, Washington"), Washington. The Terrapins beat [Houston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston_Cougars_men's_basketball "Houston Cougars men's basketball") 89–77 behind a career-high 21 points and 17 rebounds from freshman Jordan Williams,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-12) while the Spartans edged [New Mexico State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_New_Mexico_State_Aggies_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 New Mexico State Aggies men's basketball team"), 70–67. The end of the game included a controversial lane violation call on Aggies player Troy Gillenwater with 18.6 seconds left that allowed MSU to reshoot a missed free throw and extend its lead to 3.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-13)

#### Second round

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010_NCAA_Division_I_men%27s_basketball_tournament&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Second round")]

Northern Iowa stunned the nation by knocking off top overall seed Kansas, 69–67. Leading by just one in the final minute of play, Ali Farokhmanesh clinched the victory for the second time in as many games with a three-point basket that [ESPN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ESPN "ESPN")'s [Pat Forde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pat_Forde "Pat Forde") called "the greatest early-round shot in NCAA tournament history."[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-14) The win was significant for several reasons: it marked the Panthers' first trip ever to the Sweet Sixteen, and was the first time in six years a No. 1 seed was eliminated in the round of 32. It was also the first time since 1962 that a team from the [Missouri Valley Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri_Valley_Conference "Missouri Valley Conference") had defeated a top seed in the Tournament.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-15) Meanwhile, Michigan State lost guard [Kalin Lucas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalin_Lucas "Kalin Lucas") to a leg injury late in the first half of its game with Maryland. Michigan State extended its halftime lead of NINE to 16 in the second half before falling behind by one late after succumbing to Maryland's relentless pressure defense and some spectacular plays by [Greivis Vásquez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greivis_V%C3%A1squez "Greivis Vásquez"). But [Korie Lucious](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korie_Lucious "Korie Lucious") kept MSU from losing the game, hitting a 3-pointer as time ran out to lift his team past the Terrapins, 85–83.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-16) Lucas' injury proved to be a torn [Achilles tendon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Achilles_tendon "Achilles tendon"), putting the junior out of action for up to six months.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-17)

For the third time in four years, Tennessee made it to the regional semifinals with their 83–68 win over Ohio. J. P. Prince scored 18 points for the Volunteers, while [Scotty Hopson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scotty_Hopson "Scotty Hopson") added 17.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-18) In Milwaukee, Ohio State's [Evan Turner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evan_Turner "Evan Turner") bounced back from his off-night in the first round, nearly recording a triple-double (24 points, 9 rebounds and 9 assists) as the Buckeyes downed Georgia Tech 75–66.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-19)

### West Region

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010_NCAA_Division_I_men%27s_basketball_tournament&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: West Region")]

#### First round

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010_NCAA_Division_I_men%27s_basketball_tournament&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: First round")]

For the second time in three years, the [Vanderbilt Commodores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanderbilt_Commodores_men's_basketball "Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball") were victims of the upset, losing to [Murray State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murray_State_Racers "Murray State Racers") on a [Danero Thomas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danero_Thomas "Danero Thomas") shot with time expiring, 66–65, in [San Jose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Jose,_California "San Jose, California"), California. Like 2008, when they lost to [Siena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siena_Saints_men's_basketball "Siena Saints men's basketball"), Vandy was seeded fourth against the Racers.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-21) Murray State advanced to face fifth-seeded [Butler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Butler_Bulldogs_men's_basketball "Butler Bulldogs men's basketball"), who defeated [UTEP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UTEP_Miners_men's_basketball "UTEP Miners men's basketball"), 77–59, after trailing 33–27 at the half. Shelvin Mack led the Bulldogs with 25 points.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-22)

Meanwhile, the [Florida Gators](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Gators_men's_basketball "Florida Gators men's basketball") rallied from a 13-point deficit in Oklahoma City to send their game with [BYU](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BYU_Cougars_men's_basketball "BYU Cougars men's basketball") to two overtimes. But Florida player Chandler Parsons missed chances to win the game at the end of regulation and the first overtime, and BYU's [Jimmer Fredette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette "Jimmer Fredette") sealed the 99–92 win with a pair of threes in the second overtime. Fredette finished with 37 points, the eighth time that year he'd scored over 30.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-23) BYU advanced to play [Kansas State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_State_Wildcats_men's_basketball "Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball"), who had little trouble with the [North Texas Mean Green](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Texas_Mean_Green "North Texas Mean Green"), winning 82–62.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-24)

Five years after [Vermont](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vermont_Catamounts "Vermont Catamounts") upset [Syracuse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syracuse_Orange_men's_basketball "Syracuse Orange men's basketball"), the two teams met again in the Big Dance, this time in [Buffalo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buffalo,_New_York "Buffalo, New York"), New York. Unlike the 2005 game, however, Syracuse was able to shut down the Catamounts, winning 79–56. Five players scored in double digits for the Orange.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-25) They advanced to play [Gonzaga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gonzaga_Bulldogs_men's_basketball "Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball"). The Bulldogs had an 18-point led against [Florida State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_State_Seminoles_men's_basketball "Florida State Seminoles men's basketball"), but the Seminoles cut it to five with 2:21 remaining. The Zags survived FSU's comeback, however, by making 8 of 10 free throws down the stretch to seal a 67–60 win.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-26)

The last two slots in the West went to [Pittsburgh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh_Panthers_men's_basketball "Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball") and [Xavier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xavier_Musketeers_men's_basketball "Xavier Musketeers men's basketball"). It was a close game between Pittsburgh and [Oakland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oakland_Golden_Grizzlies_men's_basketball "Oakland Golden Grizzlies men's basketball") in Milwaukee until Grizzlies forward Derick Nelson received an elbow from Gary McGhee of the Panthers, opening a cut over his left eye that began spurting blood. Immediately after Nelson's departure, Pitt went on a 19–2 run. The Panthers held Oakland to 33 percent in their 89–66 victory.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-27) As for Xavier, they beat [Minnesota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minnesota_Golden_Gophers_men's_basketball "Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball"), 65–54. [Jordan Crawford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan_Crawford "Jordan Crawford"), the Xavier player who made national headlines the previous summer when he dunked on [LeBron James](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LeBron_James "LeBron James") during a training camp held by the [Cleveland Cavaliers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland_Cavaliers "Cleveland Cavaliers") superstar,[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-28) scored 28 points for the Musketeers, 17 of those came in the second half.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-29)

#### Second round

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010_NCAA_Division_I_men%27s_basketball_tournament&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Second round")]

Murray State had another chance at an upset against Butler, but a 3-point play by Bulldog [Ronald Nored](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Nored "Ronald Nored") dashed those hopes, along with [Gordon Hayward](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gordon_Hayward "Gordon Hayward") deflecting a Racers pass. Butler won 54–52.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-30) The Bulldogs' next opponent, top-seeded Syracuse, rolled over Gonzaga, 87–65, with [Wes Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wesley_Johnson_(basketball) "Wesley Johnson (basketball)") scoring a career best 31 points and pulling 14 rebounds.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-31)

2 seed Kansas State fell behind to BYU early, trailing 10–0 to start the game. But the Wildcats would pull ahead with 4:21 to go in the first half and never relinquished the lead after that, advancing to the next round with an 84–72 win. K-State's [Jacob Pullen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacob_Pullen "Jacob Pullen") had a career-high 34 points.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-32) And third-seeded Pitt was eliminated by Xavier, 71–68. Jordan Crawford had 27 points for the Musketeers.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-33)

In what Gregg Doyel of [CBSSports.com](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBSSports.com "CBSSports.com") called "one of the best games in the history of the Sweet 16", Kansas State downed Xavier, 101–96, in double overtime in [Salt Lake City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salt_Lake_City "Salt Lake City").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-34) The Musketeers' [Terrell Holloway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tu_Holloway "Tu Holloway") made three free throws with 5 seconds remaining in regulation to pull Xavier even with the Wildcats. Down 3 again with the first overtime winding down, [Jordan Crawford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan_Crawford "Jordan Crawford") nailed a 35-foot shot to extend the game further. [Jacob Pullen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacob_Pullen "Jacob Pullen") then hit a pair of threes in the second overtime to push K-State over the top.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-35)

Syracuse became the second number-one seed to fall, as Butler claimed its first-ever trip to the Elite Eight. The 63–59 win brought the Bulldogs within one win of playing the Final Four in their home city. Trailing by four with 5:23 left, Butler held the Orange scoreless for nearly five minutes, while scoring 11 points of their own, including a 3-point shot by Willie Veasley that bounced high off the rim before hitting the backboard and eventually falling through the net. The win marked Butler's 23rd in a row.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-36)

In [New Orleans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans "New Orleans"), [Ishmael Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ishmael_Smith "Ishmael Smith") scored a 17-foot jumper with 1.3 seconds left in overtime as [Wake Forest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wake_Forest_Demon_Deacons_men's_basketball "Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball") defeated [Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Longhorns_men's_basketball "Texas Longhorns men's basketball"), 81–80. The Longhorns, who had been ranked number one as recently as January, but fell to an 8 seed in the tournament, twice trailed by double digits before rallying, then held an eight-point lead before falling.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-38) Wake Forest advanced to face top-seeded Kentucky, who breezed past [East Tennessee State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Tennessee_State_Buccaneers "East Tennessee State Buccaneers"), 100–71.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-39)

A basket by [Quincy Pondexter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quincy_Pondexter "Quincy Pondexter") with 1.7 seconds remaining helped the [Washington Huskies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Huskies_men's_basketball "Washington Huskies men's basketball") past [Marquette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marquette_Golden_Eagles_men's_basketball "Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball"), 80–78, in San Jose. Washington had trailed by 15 with over 13 minutes to go in the second half.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-40) The Huskies advanced to face [New Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Lobos_men's_basketball "New Mexico Lobos men's basketball"), who beat the [Montana Grizzlies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montana_Grizzlies "Montana Grizzlies"), 62–57. Roman Martinez scored 19 points for the Lobos, while [Darington Hobson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darington_Hobson "Darington Hobson") had 11 points, 11 rebounds and six assists despite playing with a sprained left wrist.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-41)

[Louis Dale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_Dale "Louis Dale"), [Ryan Wittman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Wittman "Ryan Wittman") and [Jeff Foote](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeff_Foote "Jeff Foote"), all seniors for the Big Red, scored 21, 20 and 16 points respectively, and Cornell shot 56 percent from the field overall, making 8 of their first 10 shots and shooting 68 percent in the first half. It was the first tournament win in Big Red history.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-42) The [Wisconsin Badgers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wisconsin_Badgers_men's_basketball "Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball"), who Cornell drew next, managed to avoid getting upset itself, beating [Wofford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wofford_Terriers_men's_basketball "Wofford Terriers men's basketball") in a low-scoring affair, 53–49. The **2010 [NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament")** involved 65 teams playing in a [single-elimination tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single-elimination_tournament "Single-elimination tournament") that determined the [National Collegiate Athletic Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Collegiate_Athletic_Association "National Collegiate Athletic Association") (NCAA) [Division I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NCAA_Division_I "NCAA Division I") men's [basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_basketball "College basketball") national champion for the [2009–10 basketball season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_season "2009–10 NCAA Division I men's basketball season"). The 72nd annual edition of the tournament began on March 16, 2010, and concluded with the [championship game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Division_I_Basketball_Championship_Game "2010 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship Game") on April 5, at [Lucas Oil Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucas_Oil_Stadium "Lucas Oil Stadium") in [Indianapolis, Indiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indianapolis "Indianapolis").

The Final Four consisted of [Duke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Duke_Blue_Devils_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team"), making their first appearance since [2004](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "2004 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament"), [West Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_West_Virginia_Mountaineers_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball team"), who were making their second appearance and first since [1959](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1959_NCAA_University_Division_basketball_tournament "1959 NCAA University Division basketball tournament"), [Butler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Butler_Bulldogs_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Butler Bulldogs men's basketball team"), considered the host school and making their first ever appearance, and [Michigan State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Michigan_State_Spartans_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team"), the national runner-up from [2009](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "2009 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament") appearing in the Final Four for the sixth time under head coach [Tom Izzo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Izzo "Tom Izzo").

When Duke and Butler played each other in the tournament final, it was the first title game between private universities in 25 years ([Villanova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1984%E2%80%9385_Villanova_Wildcats_men's_basketball_team "1984–85 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team") and [Georgetown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1984%E2%80%9385_Georgetown_Hoyas_men's_basketball_team "1984–85 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team") met in [1985](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1985_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "1985 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament")), and the fifth such match-up in history ([1942](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1942_NCAA_basketball_tournament "1942 NCAA basketball tournament"), [1954](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1954_NCAA_basketball_tournament "1954 NCAA basketball tournament"), and [1955](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1955_NCAA_basketball_tournament "1955 NCAA basketball tournament") having been the other years). Duke defeated Butler 61–59 in the championship game as [Gordon Hayward](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gordon_Hayward "Gordon Hayward")'s last second desperation shot clanged off the rim. It was Duke's first national championship since [2001](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "2001 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament") and fourth overall.

Entering the tournament, the top four seeds were [Kansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Kansas_Jayhawks_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team"), Duke, [Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Kentucky_Wildcats_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team"), and [Syracuse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Syracuse_Orange_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Syracuse Orange men's basketball team"). Kansas entered the Tournament as the overall No. 1 seed but was defeated in the opening weekend by [Northern Iowa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Northern_Iowa_Panthers_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Northern Iowa Panthers men's basketball team"), the No. 9 seed in the Midwest region. Northern Iowa was one of four teams seeded lower than No. 8 to advance to the Sweet Sixteen, joining the East Region's No. 11 seed [Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Washington_Huskies_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Washington Huskies men's basketball team"), No. 12 seed [Cornell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Cornell_Big_Red_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Cornell Big Red men's basketball team") and the South Region's No. 10 seed [Saint Mary's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Saint_Mary's_Gaels_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Saint Mary's Gaels men's basketball team").

For the first time since [2006](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "2006 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament"), a No. 14 seed advanced out of the first round as [Ohio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ohio_Bobcats_men's_basketball "Ohio Bobcats men's basketball") defeated [Georgetown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgetown_Hoyas_men's_basketball "Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball"). The No. 13 seed in the West Region, [Murray State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murray_State_Racers_men's_basketball "Murray State Racers men's basketball"), defeated No. 4-seeded [Vanderbilt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanderbilt_Commodores_men's_basketball "Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball"), marking the second consecutive appearance for the Commodores where they lost as a No. 4 seed. Murray State very nearly upset Butler in their next game, losing by two points.

One of the more exciting games of the tournament was played at the West Regional in [Salt Lake City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salt_Lake_City "Salt Lake City"), as No. 6 [Xavier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xavier_Musketeers_men's_basketball "Xavier Musketeers men's basketball") took No. 2 [Kansas State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_State_Wildcats_men's_basketball "Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball") to two overtimes before falling 101–96. [Jordan Crawford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan_Crawford "Jordan Crawford") hit a three-pointer with seconds remaining in the first overtime period to force a second.

## Tournament procedure

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010_NCAA_Division_I_men%27s_basketball_tournament&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Tournament procedure")]

Further information: [NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship §Format history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NCAA_Men's_Division_I_Basketball_Championship#Format_history "NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship")

A total of 65 teams were selected for the tournament. Thirty one of the teams earned automatic bids by winning their [conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_NCAA_conferences "List of NCAA conferences") tournaments. The automatic bid of the [Ivy League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivy_League "Ivy League"), which at the time did not conduct a postseason tournament, went to [Cornell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Cornell_Big_Red_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Cornell Big Red men's basketball team"), its regular season champion. The remaining 34 teams were granted at-large bids, which were extended by the NCAA Selection Committee.

Two teams played an opening-round game, popularly called the play-in game; the winner of that game advanced to the main draw of the tournament and played a top seed in one of the regionals. The 2010 game was played on March 16 at [University of Dayton Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Dayton_Arena "University of Dayton Arena") in [Dayton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dayton,_Ohio "Dayton, Ohio"), Ohio, as it has been since its inception in [2001](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "2001 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament").

All 64 teams were seeded 1 to 16 within their regions; the winner of the play-in game automatically received a 16 seed. The [Selection Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NCAA_basketball_tournament_selection_process "NCAA basketball tournament selection process") seeded the entire field from 1 to 65. [UCLA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UCLA_Bruins "UCLA Bruins") athletic director [Dan Guerrero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Guerrero "Dan Guerrero") took over as chair of the Division I Men's Basketball Committee.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-1)

Defending champion [North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_North_Carolina_Tar_Heels_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team") did not qualify for the Tournament, while two schools made their first post-season appearance: [Southern Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Conference "Southern Conference") champion [Wofford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Wofford_Terriers_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Wofford Terriers men's basketball team") and [SWAC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southwestern_Athletic_Conference "Southwestern Athletic Conference") champion [Arkansas-Pine Bluff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arkansas%E2%80%93Pine_Bluff_Golden_Lions_men's_basketball "Arkansas–Pine Bluff Golden Lions men's basketball"). [Conference USA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conference_USA "Conference USA") champion [Houston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Houston_Cougars_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Houston Cougars men's basketball team") made its first NCAA Tournament appearance in 18 years.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-2)

## Game summaries

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010_NCAA_Division_I_men%27s_basketball_tournament&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Game summaries")]

### Midwest Region

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010_NCAA_Division_I_men%27s_basketball_tournament&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Midwest Region")]

#### First round

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010_NCAA_Division_I_men%27s_basketball_tournament&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: First round")]

The biggest upset of the first day came in [Providence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Providence,_Rhode_Island "Providence, Rhode Island"), Rhode Island, where 14th-seeded [Ohio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Ohio_Bobcats_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Ohio Bobcats men's basketball team") defeated third-seeded [Georgetown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Georgetown_Hoyas_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team") in convincing fashion, 97–83, for their first Tournament win since [1983](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1983_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "1983 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament"), when they ousted [Illinois State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois_State_Redbirds_men's_basketball "Illinois State Redbirds men's basketball") in the first round of that Tournament. [Armon Bassett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armon_Bassett "Armon Bassett") scored 32 points for the Bobcats, who shot 57 percent from the field and made 13 of 23 3-pointers.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-6) They advanced to face [Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Tennessee_Volunteers_basketball_team "2009–10 Tennessee Volunteers basketball team"), the sixth seed in the region. The Volunteers held off 11th seed [San Diego State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_San_Diego_State_Aztecs_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 San Diego State Aztecs men's basketball team"), 62–59, on head coach [Bruce Pearl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruce_Pearl "Bruce Pearl")'s 50th birthday. [J. P. Prince](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J._P._Prince "J. P. Prince") and Melvin Goins scored 15 points each for Tennessee.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-7)

In [Oklahoma City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oklahoma_City "Oklahoma City"), [Ali Farokhmanesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ali_Farokhmanesh "Ali Farokhmanesh") drilled a three-pointer with 4.9 seconds remaining to lift ninth-seeded [Northern Iowa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Northern_Iowa_Panthers_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Northern Iowa Panthers men's basketball team") over [UNLV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_UNLV_Runnin'_Rebels_basketball_team "2009–10 UNLV Runnin' Rebels basketball team"). It was the Panthers first Tournament win since [1990](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "1990 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-8) UNI advanced to face top-seeded [Kansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Kansas_Jayhawks_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team"). The top seed withheld an effort by [Lehigh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lehigh_Mountain_Hawks_men's_basketball "Lehigh Mountain Hawks men's basketball"), trailing the 16th seed early in the game and leading by just six at halftime before pulling away midway in the second half for a 90–74 win.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-9)

On the second day of play, 10th-seeded [Georgia Tech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Georgia_Tech_Yellow_Jackets_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball team") failed to make a single field goal in the final 8:19 of play, but sank 13 free throws to hold off No. 7 [Oklahoma State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Oklahoma_State_Cowboys_basketball_team "2009–10 Oklahoma State Cowboys basketball team"), 64–59, in [Milwaukee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milwaukee "Milwaukee"). [Gani Lawal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gani_Lawal "Gani Lawal") led Georgia Tech with 14 points.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-10) The Yellow Jackets advanced to play [Ohio State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Ohio_State_Buckeyes_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball team"), who defeated [UC Santa Barbara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_UC_Santa_Barbara_Gauchos_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 UC Santa Barbara Gauchos men's basketball team") 68–51. Buckeye star [Evan Turner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evan_Turner "Evan Turner") struggled from the field, shooting 2–13 and scoring nine points, and the Gauchos put up a fight, playing from behind most of the game.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-11)

Rounding out the Midwest bracket were [Maryland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Maryland_Terrapins_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Maryland Terrapins men's basketball team") and [Michigan State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Michigan_State_Spartans_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team") in [Spokane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spokane,_Washington "Spokane, Washington"), Washington. The Terrapins beat [Houston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston_Cougars_men's_basketball "Houston Cougars men's basketball") 89–77 behind a career-high 21 points and 17 rebounds from freshman Jordan Williams,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-12) while the Spartans edged [New Mexico State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_New_Mexico_State_Aggies_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 New Mexico State Aggies men's basketball team"), 70–67. The end of the game included a controversial lane violation call on Aggies player Troy Gillenwater with 18.6 seconds left that allowed MSU to reshoot a missed free throw and extend its lead to 3.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-13)

#### Second round

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010_NCAA_Division_I_men%27s_basketball_tournament&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Second round")]

Northern Iowa stunned the nation by knocking off top overall seed Kansas, 69–67. Leading by just one in the final minute of play, Ali Farokhmanesh clinched the victory for the second time in as many games with a three-point basket that [ESPN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ESPN "ESPN")'s [Pat Forde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pat_Forde "Pat Forde") called "the greatest early-round shot in NCAA tournament history."[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-14) The win was significant for several reasons: it marked the Panthers' first trip ever to the Sweet Sixteen, and was the first time in six years a No. 1 seed was eliminated in the round of 32. It was also the first time since 1962 that a team from the [Missouri Valley Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri_Valley_Conference "Missouri Valley Conference") had defeated a top seed in the Tournament.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-15) Meanwhile, Michigan State lost guard [Kalin Lucas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalin_Lucas "Kalin Lucas") to a leg injury late in the first half of its game with Maryland. Michigan State extended its halftime lead of NINE to 16 in the second half before falling behind by one late after succumbing to Maryland's relentless pressure defense and some spectacular plays by [Greivis Vásquez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greivis_V%C3%A1squez "Greivis Vásquez"). But [Korie Lucious](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korie_Lucious "Korie Lucious") kept MSU from losing the game, hitting a 3-pointer as time ran out to lift his team past the Terrapins, 85–83.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-16) Lucas' injury proved to be a torn [Achilles tendon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Achilles_tendon "Achilles tendon"), putting the junior out of action for up to six months.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-17)

For the third time in four years, Tennessee made it to the regional semifinals with their 83–68 win over Ohio. J. P. Prince scored 18 points for the Volunteers, while [Scotty Hopson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scotty_Hopson "Scotty Hopson") added 17.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-18) In Milwaukee, Ohio State's [Evan Turner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evan_Turner "Evan Turner") bounced back from his off-night in the first round, nearly recording a triple-double (24 points, 9 rebounds and 9 assists) as the Buckeyes downed Georgia Tech 75–66.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-19)
