### West Region

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010_NCAA_Division_I_men%27s_basketball_tournament&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: West Region")]

#### First round

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010_NCAA_Division_I_men%27s_basketball_tournament&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: First round")]

For the second time in three years, the [Vanderbilt Commodores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanderbilt_Commodores_men's_basketball "Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball") were victims of the upset, losing to [Murray State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murray_State_Racers "Murray State Racers") on a [Danero Thomas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danero_Thomas "Danero Thomas") shot with time expiring, 66–65, in [San Jose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Jose,_California "San Jose, California"), California. Like 2008, when they lost to [Siena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siena_Saints_men's_basketball "Siena Saints men's basketball"), Vandy was seeded fourth against the Racers.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-21) Murray State advanced to face fifth-seeded [Butler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Butler_Bulldogs_men's_basketball "Butler Bulldogs men's basketball"), who defeated [UTEP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UTEP_Miners_men's_basketball "UTEP Miners men's basketball"), 77–59, after trailing 33–27 at the half. Shelvin Mack led the Bulldogs with 25 points.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-22)

Meanwhile, the [Florida Gators](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Gators_men's_basketball "Florida Gators men's basketball") rallied from a 13-point deficit in Oklahoma City to send their game with [BYU](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BYU_Cougars_men's_basketball "BYU Cougars men's basketball") to two overtimes. But Florida player Chandler Parsons missed chances to win the game at the end of regulation and the first overtime, and BYU's [Jimmer Fredette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette "Jimmer Fredette") sealed the 99–92 win with a pair of threes in the second overtime. Fredette finished with 37 points, the eighth time that year he'd scored over 30.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-23) BYU advanced to play [Kansas State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_State_Wildcats_men's_basketball "Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball"), who had little trouble with the [North Texas Mean Green](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Texas_Mean_Green "North Texas Mean Green"), winning 82–62.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-24)

Five years after [Vermont](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vermont_Catamounts "Vermont Catamounts") upset [Syracuse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syracuse_Orange_men's_basketball "Syracuse Orange men's basketball"), the two teams met again in the Big Dance, this time in [Buffalo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buffalo,_New_York "Buffalo, New York"), New York. Unlike the 2005 game, however, Syracuse was able to shut down the Catamounts, winning 79–56. Five players scored in double digits for the Orange.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-25) They advanced to play [Gonzaga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gonzaga_Bulldogs_men's_basketball "Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball"). The Bulldogs had an 18-point led against [Florida State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_State_Seminoles_men's_basketball "Florida State Seminoles men's basketball"), but the Seminoles cut it to five with 2:21 remaining. The Zags survived FSU's comeback, however, by making 8 of 10 free throws down the stretch to seal a 67–60 win.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-26)

The last two slots in the West went to [Pittsburgh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh_Panthers_men's_basketball "Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball") and [Xavier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xavier_Musketeers_men's_basketball "Xavier Musketeers men's basketball"). It was a close game between Pittsburgh and [Oakland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oakland_Golden_Grizzlies_men's_basketball "Oakland Golden Grizzlies men's basketball") in Milwaukee until Grizzlies forward Derick Nelson received an elbow from Gary McGhee of the Panthers, opening a cut over his left eye that began spurting blood. Immediately after Nelson's departure, Pitt went on a 19–2 run. The Panthers held Oakland to 33 percent in their 89–66 victory.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-27) As for Xavier, they beat [Minnesota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minnesota_Golden_Gophers_men's_basketball "Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball"), 65–54. [Jordan Crawford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan_Crawford "Jordan Crawford"), the Xavier player who made national headlines the previous summer when he dunked on [LeBron James](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LeBron_James "LeBron James") during a training camp held by the [Cleveland Cavaliers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland_Cavaliers "Cleveland Cavaliers") superstar,[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-28) scored 28 points for the Musketeers, 17 of those came in the second half.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-29)

#### Second round

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010_NCAA_Division_I_men%27s_basketball_tournament&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Second round")]

Murray State had another chance at an upset against Butler, but a 3-point play by Bulldog [Ronald Nored](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Nored "Ronald Nored") dashed those hopes, along with [Gordon Hayward](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gordon_Hayward "Gordon Hayward") deflecting a Racers pass. Butler won 54–52.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-30) The Bulldogs' next opponent, top-seeded Syracuse, rolled over Gonzaga, 87–65, with [Wes Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wesley_Johnson_(basketball) "Wesley Johnson (basketball)") scoring a career best 31 points and pulling 14 rebounds.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-31)

2 seed Kansas State fell behind to BYU early, trailing 10–0 to start the game. But the Wildcats would pull ahead with 4:21 to go in the first half and never relinquished the lead after that, advancing to the next round with an 84–72 win. K-State's [Jacob Pullen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacob_Pullen "Jacob Pullen") had a career-high 34 points.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-32) And third-seeded Pitt was eliminated by Xavier, 71–68. Jordan Crawford had 27 points for the Musketeers.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Basketball_Tournament#cite_note-33)

The **2010 [NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament")** involved 65 teams playing in a [single-elimination tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single-elimination_tournament "Single-elimination tournament") that determined the [National Collegiate Athletic Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Collegiate_Athletic_Association "National Collegiate Athletic Association") (NCAA) [Division I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NCAA_Division_I "NCAA Division I") men's [basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_basketball "College basketball") national champion for the [2009–10 basketball season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_season "2009–10 NCAA Division I men's basketball season"). The 72nd annual edition of the tournament began on March 16, 2010, and concluded with the [championship game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Division_I_Basketball_Championship_Game "2010 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship Game") on April 5, at [Lucas Oil Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucas_Oil_Stadium "Lucas Oil Stadium") in [Indianapolis, Indiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indianapolis "Indianapolis").

The Final Four consisted of [Duke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Duke_Blue_Devils_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team"), making their first appearance since [2004](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "2004 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament"), [West Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_West_Virginia_Mountaineers_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball team"), who were making their second appearance and first since [1959](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1959_NCAA_University_Division_basketball_tournament "1959 NCAA University Division basketball tournament"), [Butler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Butler_Bulldogs_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Butler Bulldogs men's basketball team"), considered the host school and making their first ever appearance, and [Michigan State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Michigan_State_Spartans_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team"), the national runner-up from [2009](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "2009 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament") appearing in the Final Four for the sixth time under head coach [Tom Izzo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Izzo "Tom Izzo").

When Duke and Butler played each other in the tournament final, it was the first title game between private universities in 25 years ([Villanova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1984%E2%80%9385_Villanova_Wildcats_men's_basketball_team "1984–85 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team") and [Georgetown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1984%E2%80%9385_Georgetown_Hoyas_men's_basketball_team "1984–85 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team") met in [1985](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1985_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "1985 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament")), and the fifth such match-up in history ([1942](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1942_NCAA_basketball_tournament "1942 NCAA basketball tournament"), [1954](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1954_NCAA_basketball_tournament "1954 NCAA basketball tournament"), and [1955](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1955_NCAA_basketball_tournament "1955 NCAA basketball tournament") having been the other years). Duke defeated Butler 61–59 in the championship game as [Gordon Hayward](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gordon_Hayward "Gordon Hayward")'s last second desperation shot clanged off the rim. It was Duke's first national championship since [2001](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "2001 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament") and fourth overall.

Entering the tournament, the top four seeds were [Kansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Kansas_Jayhawks_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team"), Duke, [Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Kentucky_Wildcats_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team"), and [Syracuse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Syracuse_Orange_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Syracuse Orange men's basketball team"). Kansas entered the Tournament as the overall No. 1 seed but was defeated in the opening weekend by [Northern Iowa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Northern_Iowa_Panthers_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Northern Iowa Panthers men's basketball team"), the No. 9 seed in the Midwest region. Northern Iowa was one of four teams seeded lower than No. 8 to advance to the Sweet Sixteen, joining the East Region's No. 11 seed [Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Washington_Huskies_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Washington Huskies men's basketball team"), No. 12 seed [Cornell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Cornell_Big_Red_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Cornell Big Red men's basketball team") and the South Region's No. 10 seed [Saint Mary's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Saint_Mary's_Gaels_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Saint Mary's Gaels men's basketball team").

For the first time since [2006](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "2006 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament"), a No. 14 seed advanced out of the first round as [Ohio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ohio_Bobcats_men's_basketball "Ohio Bobcats men's basketball") defeated [Georgetown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgetown_Hoyas_men's_basketball "Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball"). The No. 13 seed in the West Region, [Murray State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murray_State_Racers_men's_basketball "Murray State Racers men's basketball"), defeated No. 4-seeded [Vanderbilt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanderbilt_Commodores_men's_basketball "Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball"), marking the second consecutive appearance for the Commodores where they lost as a No. 4 seed. Murray State very nearly upset Butler in their next game, losing by two points.

One of the more exciting games of the tournament was played at the West Regional in [Salt Lake City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salt_Lake_City "Salt Lake City"), as No. 6 [Xavier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xavier_Musketeers_men's_basketball "Xavier Musketeers men's basketball") took No. 2 [Kansas State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_State_Wildcats_men's_basketball "Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball") to two overtimes before falling 101–96. [Jordan Crawford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan_Crawford "Jordan Crawford") hit a three-pointer with seconds remaining in the first overtime period to force a second.

## Tournament procedure

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010_NCAA_Division_I_men%27s_basketball_tournament&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Tournament procedure")]

Further information: [NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship §Format history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NCAA_Men's_Division_I_Basketball_Championship#Format_history "NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship")

A total of 65 teams were selected for the tournament. Thirty one of the teams earned automatic bids by winning their [conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_NCAA_conferences "List of NCAA conferences") tournaments. The automatic bid of the [Ivy League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivy_League "Ivy League"), which at the time did not conduct a postseason tournament, went to [Cornell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Cornell_Big_Red_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Cornell Big Red men's basketball team"), its regular season champion. The remaining 34 teams were granted at-large bids, which were extended by the NCAA Selection Committee.

Two teams played an opening-round game, popularly called the play-in game; the winner of that game advanced to the main draw of the tournament and played a top seed in one of the regionals. The 2010 game was played on March 16 at [University of Dayton Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Dayton_Arena "University of Dayton Arena") in [Dayton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dayton,_Ohio "Dayton, Ohio"), Ohio, as it has been since its inception in [2001](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "2001 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament").

All 64 teams were seeded 1 to 16 within their regions; the winner of the play-in game automatically received a 16 seed. The [Selection Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NCAA_basketball_tournament_selection_process "NCAA basketball tournament selection process") seeded the entire field from 1 to 65. [UCLA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UCLA_Bruins "UCLA Bruins") athletic director [Dan Guerrero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Guerrero "Dan Guerrero") took over as chair of the Division I Men's Basketball Committee.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-1)

Defending champion [North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_North_Carolina_Tar_Heels_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team") did not qualify for the Tournament, while two schools made their first post-season appearance: [Southern Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Conference "Southern Conference") champion [Wofford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Wofford_Terriers_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Wofford Terriers men's basketball team") and [SWAC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southwestern_Athletic_Conference "Southwestern Athletic Conference") champion [Arkansas-Pine Bluff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arkansas%E2%80%93Pine_Bluff_Golden_Lions_men's_basketball "Arkansas–Pine Bluff Golden Lions men's basketball"). [Conference USA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conference_USA "Conference USA") champion [Houston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Houston_Cougars_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Houston Cougars men's basketball team") made its first NCAA Tournament appearance in 18 years.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-2)

## Game summaries

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010_NCAA_Division_I_men%27s_basketball_tournament&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Game summaries")]

### Midwest Region

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010_NCAA_Division_I_men%27s_basketball_tournament&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Midwest Region")]

#### First round

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010_NCAA_Division_I_men%27s_basketball_tournament&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: First round")]

The biggest upset of the first day came in [Providence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Providence,_Rhode_Island "Providence, Rhode Island"), Rhode Island, where 14th-seeded [Ohio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Ohio_Bobcats_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Ohio Bobcats men's basketball team") defeated third-seeded [Georgetown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Georgetown_Hoyas_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team") in convincing fashion, 97–83, for their first Tournament win since [1983](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1983_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "1983 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament"), when they ousted [Illinois State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois_State_Redbirds_men's_basketball "Illinois State Redbirds men's basketball") in the first round of that Tournament. [Armon Bassett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armon_Bassett "Armon Bassett") scored 32 points for the Bobcats, who shot 57 percent from the field and made 13 of 23 3-pointers.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-6) They advanced to face [Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Tennessee_Volunteers_basketball_team "2009–10 Tennessee Volunteers basketball team"), the sixth seed in the region. The Volunteers held off 11th seed [San Diego State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_San_Diego_State_Aztecs_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 San Diego State Aztecs men's basketball team"), 62–59, on head coach [Bruce Pearl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruce_Pearl "Bruce Pearl")'s 50th birthday. [J. P. Prince](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J._P._Prince "J. P. Prince") and Melvin Goins scored 15 points each for Tennessee.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-7)

In [Oklahoma City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oklahoma_City "Oklahoma City"), [Ali Farokhmanesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ali_Farokhmanesh "Ali Farokhmanesh") drilled a three-pointer with 4.9 seconds remaining to lift ninth-seeded [Northern Iowa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Northern_Iowa_Panthers_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Northern Iowa Panthers men's basketball team") over [UNLV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_UNLV_Runnin'_Rebels_basketball_team "2009–10 UNLV Runnin' Rebels basketball team"). It was the Panthers first Tournament win since [1990](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "1990 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-8) UNI advanced to face top-seeded [Kansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Kansas_Jayhawks_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team"). The top seed withheld an effort by [Lehigh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lehigh_Mountain_Hawks_men's_basketball "Lehigh Mountain Hawks men's basketball"), trailing the 16th seed early in the game and leading by just six at halftime before pulling away midway in the second half for a 90–74 win.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-9)

On the second day of play, 10th-seeded [Georgia Tech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Georgia_Tech_Yellow_Jackets_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball team") failed to make a single field goal in the final 8:19 of play, but sank 13 free throws to hold off No. 7 [Oklahoma State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Oklahoma_State_Cowboys_basketball_team "2009–10 Oklahoma State Cowboys basketball team"), 64–59, in [Milwaukee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milwaukee "Milwaukee"). [Gani Lawal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gani_Lawal "Gani Lawal") led Georgia Tech with 14 points.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-10) The Yellow Jackets advanced to play [Ohio State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Ohio_State_Buckeyes_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball team"), who defeated [UC Santa Barbara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_UC_Santa_Barbara_Gauchos_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 UC Santa Barbara Gauchos men's basketball team") 68–51. Buckeye star [Evan Turner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evan_Turner "Evan Turner") struggled from the field, shooting 2–13 and scoring nine points, and the Gauchos put up a fight, playing from behind most of the game.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-11)

Rounding out the Midwest bracket were [Maryland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Maryland_Terrapins_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Maryland Terrapins men's basketball team") and [Michigan State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Michigan_State_Spartans_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team") in [Spokane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spokane,_Washington "Spokane, Washington"), Washington. The Terrapins beat [Houston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston_Cougars_men's_basketball "Houston Cougars men's basketball") 89–77 behind a career-high 21 points and 17 rebounds from freshman Jordan Williams,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-12) while the Spartans edged [New Mexico State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_New_Mexico_State_Aggies_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 New Mexico State Aggies men's basketball team"), 70–67. The end of the game included a controversial lane violation call on Aggies player Troy Gillenwater with 18.6 seconds left that allowed MSU to reshoot a missed free throw and extend its lead to 3.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-13)

#### Second round

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010_NCAA_Division_I_men%27s_basketball_tournament&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Second round")]

Northern Iowa stunned the nation by knocking off top overall seed Kansas, 69–67. Leading by just one in the final minute of play, Ali Farokhmanesh clinched the victory for the second time in as many games with a three-point basket that [ESPN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ESPN "ESPN")'s [Pat Forde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pat_Forde "Pat Forde") called "the greatest early-round shot in NCAA tournament history."[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-14) The win was significant for several reasons: it marked the Panthers' first trip ever to the Sweet Sixteen, and was the first time in six years a No. 1 seed was eliminated in the round of 32. It was also the first time since 1962 that a team from the [Missouri Valley Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri_Valley_Conference "Missouri Valley Conference") had defeated a top seed in the Tournament.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-15) Meanwhile, Michigan State lost guard [Kalin Lucas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalin_Lucas "Kalin Lucas") to a leg injury late in the first half of its game with Maryland. Michigan State extended its halftime lead of NINE to 16 in the second half before falling behind by one late after succumbing to Maryland's relentless pressure defense and some spectacular plays by [Greivis Vásquez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greivis_V%C3%A1squez "Greivis Vásquez"). But [Korie Lucious](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korie_Lucious "Korie Lucious") kept MSU from losing the game, hitting a 3-pointer as time ran out to lift his team past the Terrapins, 85–83.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-16) Lucas' injury proved to be a torn [Achilles tendon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Achilles_tendon "Achilles tendon"), putting the junior out of action for up to six months.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-17)

For the third time in four years, Tennessee made it to the regional semifinals with their 83–68 win over Ohio. J. P. ### West Region

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010_NCAA_Division_I_men%27s_basketball_tournament&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: West Region")]

#### First round

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010_NCAA_Division_I_men%27s_basketball_tournament&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: First round")]

For the second time in three years, the [Vanderbilt Commodores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanderbilt_Commodores_men's_basketball "Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball") were victims of the upset, losing to [Murray State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murray_State_Racers "Murray State Racers") on a [Danero Thomas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danero_Thomas "Danero Thomas") shot with time expiring, 66–65, in [San Jose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Jose,_California "San Jose, California"), California. Like 2008, when they lost to [Siena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siena_Saints_men's_basketball "Siena Saints men's basketball"), Vandy was seeded fourth against the Racers.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-21) Murray State advanced to face fifth-seeded [Butler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Butler_Bulldogs_men's_basketball "Butler Bulldogs men's basketball"), who defeated [UTEP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UTEP_Miners_men's_basketball "UTEP Miners men's basketball"), 77–59, after trailing 33–27 at the half. Shelvin Mack led the Bulldogs with 25 points.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-22)

Meanwhile, the [Florida Gators](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Gators_men's_basketball "Florida Gators men's basketball") rallied from a 13-point deficit in Oklahoma City to send their game with [BYU](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BYU_Cougars_men's_basketball "BYU Cougars men's basketball") to two overtimes. But Florida player Chandler Parsons missed chances to win the game at the end of regulation and the first overtime, and BYU's [Jimmer Fredette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmer_Fredette "Jimmer Fredette") sealed the 99–92 win with a pair of threes in the second overtime. Fredette finished with 37 points, the eighth time that year he'd scored over 30.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-23) BYU advanced to play [Kansas State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_State_Wildcats_men's_basketball "Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball"), who had little trouble with the [North Texas Mean Green](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Texas_Mean_Green "North Texas Mean Green"), winning 82–62.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-24)

Five years after [Vermont](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vermont_Catamounts "Vermont Catamounts") upset [Syracuse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syracuse_Orange_men's_basketball "Syracuse Orange men's basketball"), the two teams met again in the Big Dance, this time in [Buffalo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buffalo,_New_York "Buffalo, New York"), New York. Unlike the 2005 game, however, Syracuse was able to shut down the Catamounts, winning 79–56. Five players scored in double digits for the Orange.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-25) They advanced to play [Gonzaga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gonzaga_Bulldogs_men's_basketball "Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball"). The Bulldogs had an 18-point led against [Florida State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_State_Seminoles_men's_basketball "Florida State Seminoles men's basketball"), but the Seminoles cut it to five with 2:21 remaining. The Zags survived FSU's comeback, however, by making 8 of 10 free throws down the stretch to seal a 67–60 win.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-26)

The last two slots in the West went to [Pittsburgh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh_Panthers_men's_basketball "Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball") and [Xavier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xavier_Musketeers_men's_basketball "Xavier Musketeers men's basketball"). It was a close game between Pittsburgh and [Oakland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oakland_Golden_Grizzlies_men's_basketball "Oakland Golden Grizzlies men's basketball") in Milwaukee until Grizzlies forward Derick Nelson received an elbow from Gary McGhee of the Panthers, opening a cut over his left eye that began spurting blood. Immediately after Nelson's departure, Pitt went on a 19–2 run. The Panthers held Oakland to 33 percent in their 89–66 victory.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-27) As for Xavier, they beat [Minnesota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minnesota_Golden_Gophers_men's_basketball "Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball"), 65–54. [Jordan Crawford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan_Crawford "Jordan Crawford"), the Xavier player who made national headlines the previous summer when he dunked on [LeBron James](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LeBron_James "LeBron James") during a training camp held by the [Cleveland Cavaliers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland_Cavaliers "Cleveland Cavaliers") superstar,[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-28) scored 28 points for the Musketeers, 17 of those came in the second half.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-29)

#### Second round

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010_NCAA_Division_I_men%27s_basketball_tournament&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Second round")]

Murray State had another chance at an upset against Butler, but a 3-point play by Bulldog [Ronald Nored](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Nored "Ronald Nored") dashed those hopes, along with [Gordon Hayward](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gordon_Hayward "Gordon Hayward") deflecting a Racers pass. Butler won 54–52.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-30) The Bulldogs' next opponent, top-seeded Syracuse, rolled over Gonzaga, 87–65, with [Wes Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wesley_Johnson_(basketball) "Wesley Johnson (basketball)") scoring a career best 31 points and pulling 14 rebounds.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-31)

2 seed Kansas State fell behind to BYU early, trailing 10–0 to start the game. But the Wildcats would pull ahead with 4:21 to go in the first half and never relinquished the lead after that, advancing to the next round with an 84–72 win. K-State's [Jacob Pullen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacob_Pullen "Jacob Pullen") had a career-high 34 points.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-32) And third-seeded Pitt was eliminated by Xavier, 71–68. Jordan Crawford had 27 points for the Musketeers.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-33)

The **2010 [NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament")** involved 65 teams playing in a [single-elimination tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single-elimination_tournament "Single-elimination tournament") that determined the [National Collegiate Athletic Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Collegiate_Athletic_Association "National Collegiate Athletic Association") (NCAA) [Division I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NCAA_Division_I "NCAA Division I") men's [basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_basketball "College basketball") national champion for the [2009–10 basketball season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_season "2009–10 NCAA Division I men's basketball season"). The 72nd annual edition of the tournament began on March 16, 2010, and concluded with the [championship game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Division_I_Basketball_Championship_Game "2010 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship Game") on April 5, at [Lucas Oil Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucas_Oil_Stadium "Lucas Oil Stadium") in [Indianapolis, Indiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indianapolis "Indianapolis").

The Final Four consisted of [Duke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Duke_Blue_Devils_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team"), making their first appearance since [2004](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "2004 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament"), [West Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_West_Virginia_Mountaineers_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball team"), who were making their second appearance and first since [1959](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1959_NCAA_University_Division_basketball_tournament "1959 NCAA University Division basketball tournament"), [Butler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Butler_Bulldogs_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Butler Bulldogs men's basketball team"), considered the host school and making their first ever appearance, and [Michigan State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Michigan_State_Spartans_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team"), the national runner-up from [2009](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "2009 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament") appearing in the Final Four for the sixth time under head coach [Tom Izzo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Izzo "Tom Izzo").

When Duke and Butler played each other in the tournament final, it was the first title game between private universities in 25 years ([Villanova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1984%E2%80%9385_Villanova_Wildcats_men's_basketball_team "1984–85 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team") and [Georgetown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1984%E2%80%9385_Georgetown_Hoyas_men's_basketball_team "1984–85 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team") met in [1985](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1985_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "1985 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament")), and the fifth such match-up in history ([1942](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1942_NCAA_basketball_tournament "1942 NCAA basketball tournament"), [1954](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1954_NCAA_basketball_tournament "1954 NCAA basketball tournament"), and [1955](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1955_NCAA_basketball_tournament "1955 NCAA basketball tournament") having been the other years). Duke defeated Butler 61–59 in the championship game as [Gordon Hayward](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gordon_Hayward "Gordon Hayward")'s last second desperation shot clanged off the rim. It was Duke's first national championship since [2001](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "2001 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament") and fourth overall.

Entering the tournament, the top four seeds were [Kansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Kansas_Jayhawks_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team"), Duke, [Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Kentucky_Wildcats_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team"), and [Syracuse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Syracuse_Orange_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Syracuse Orange men's basketball team"). Kansas entered the Tournament as the overall No. 1 seed but was defeated in the opening weekend by [Northern Iowa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Northern_Iowa_Panthers_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Northern Iowa Panthers men's basketball team"), the No. 9 seed in the Midwest region. Northern Iowa was one of four teams seeded lower than No. 8 to advance to the Sweet Sixteen, joining the East Region's No. 11 seed [Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Washington_Huskies_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Washington Huskies men's basketball team"), No. 12 seed [Cornell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Cornell_Big_Red_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Cornell Big Red men's basketball team") and the South Region's No. 10 seed [Saint Mary's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Saint_Mary's_Gaels_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Saint Mary's Gaels men's basketball team").

For the first time since [2006](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "2006 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament"), a No. 14 seed advanced out of the first round as [Ohio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ohio_Bobcats_men's_basketball "Ohio Bobcats men's basketball") defeated [Georgetown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgetown_Hoyas_men's_basketball "Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball"). The No. 13 seed in the West Region, [Murray State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murray_State_Racers_men's_basketball "Murray State Racers men's basketball"), defeated No. 4-seeded [Vanderbilt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanderbilt_Commodores_men's_basketball "Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball"), marking the second consecutive appearance for the Commodores where they lost as a No. 4 seed. Murray State very nearly upset Butler in their next game, losing by two points.

One of the more exciting games of the tournament was played at the West Regional in [Salt Lake City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salt_Lake_City "Salt Lake City"), as No. 6 [Xavier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xavier_Musketeers_men's_basketball "Xavier Musketeers men's basketball") took No. 2 [Kansas State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_State_Wildcats_men's_basketball "Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball") to two overtimes before falling 101–96. [Jordan Crawford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan_Crawford "Jordan Crawford") hit a three-pointer with seconds remaining in the first overtime period to force a second.

## Tournament procedure

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010_NCAA_Division_I_men%27s_basketball_tournament&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Tournament procedure")]

Further information: [NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship §Format history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NCAA_Men's_Division_I_Basketball_Championship#Format_history "NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship")

A total of 65 teams were selected for the tournament. Thirty one of the teams earned automatic bids by winning their [conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_NCAA_conferences "List of NCAA conferences") tournaments. The automatic bid of the [Ivy League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivy_League "Ivy League"), which at the time did not conduct a postseason tournament, went to [Cornell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Cornell_Big_Red_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Cornell Big Red men's basketball team"), its regular season champion. The remaining 34 teams were granted at-large bids, which were extended by the NCAA Selection Committee.

Two teams played an opening-round game, popularly called the play-in game; the winner of that game advanced to the main draw of the tournament and played a top seed in one of the regionals. The 2010 game was played on March 16 at [University of Dayton Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Dayton_Arena "University of Dayton Arena") in [Dayton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dayton,_Ohio "Dayton, Ohio"), Ohio, as it has been since its inception in [2001](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "2001 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament").

All 64 teams were seeded 1 to 16 within their regions; the winner of the play-in game automatically received a 16 seed. The [Selection Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NCAA_basketball_tournament_selection_process "NCAA basketball tournament selection process") seeded the entire field from 1 to 65. [UCLA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UCLA_Bruins "UCLA Bruins") athletic director [Dan Guerrero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Guerrero "Dan Guerrero") took over as chair of the Division I Men's Basketball Committee.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-1)

Defending champion [North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_North_Carolina_Tar_Heels_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team") did not qualify for the Tournament, while two schools made their first post-season appearance: [Southern Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Conference "Southern Conference") champion [Wofford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Wofford_Terriers_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Wofford Terriers men's basketball team") and [SWAC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southwestern_Athletic_Conference "Southwestern Athletic Conference") champion [Arkansas-Pine Bluff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arkansas%E2%80%93Pine_Bluff_Golden_Lions_men's_basketball "Arkansas–Pine Bluff Golden Lions men's basketball"). [Conference USA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conference_USA "Conference USA") champion [Houston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Houston_Cougars_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Houston Cougars men's basketball team") made its first NCAA Tournament appearance in 18 years.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-2)

    *   [HP Pavilion at San Jose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SAP_Center "SAP Center"), [San Jose, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Jose,_California "San Jose, California") (host: [San José State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Jos%C3%A9_State_University "San José State University"))

*   March 19 and 21 
    *   [HSBC Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KeyBank_Center "KeyBank Center"), [Buffalo, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buffalo,_New_York "Buffalo, New York") (hosts: [Canisius College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canisius_College "Canisius College"), [Niagara University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Niagara_University "Niagara University"), [Metro Atlantic Athletic Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metro_Atlantic_Athletic_Conference "Metro Atlantic Athletic Conference"))

    *   [Bradley Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bradley_Center "Bradley Center"), [Milwaukee, Wisconsin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milwaukee "Milwaukee") (host: [Marquette University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marquette_University "Marquette University"))
    *   [Spokane Veterans Memorial Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spokane_Veterans_Memorial_Arena "Spokane Veterans Memorial Arena"), [Spokane, Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spokane,_Washington "Spokane, Washington") (host: [Washington State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_State_University "Washington State University"))

**Regional semifinals and finals** (Sweet Sixteen and Elite Eight)

*   March 25 and 27 
    *   **East Regional**, [Carrier Dome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carrier_Dome "Carrier Dome"), [Syracuse, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syracuse,_New_York "Syracuse, New York") (hosts: [Syracuse University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syracuse_University "Syracuse University"), [Big East Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_East_Conference_(1979%E2%80%932013) "Big East Conference (1979–2013)"))
    *   **West Regional**, [EnergySolutions Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vivint_Smart_Home_Arena "Vivint Smart Home Arena"), [Salt Lake City, Utah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salt_Lake_City "Salt Lake City") (host: [University of Utah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Utah "University of Utah"))

*   March 26 and 28 
    *   **Midwest Regional**, [Edward Jones Dome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dome_at_America's_Center "The Dome at America's Center"), [St. Louis, Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Louis "St. Louis") (host: [Missouri Valley Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri_Valley_Conference "Missouri Valley Conference"))
    *   **South Regional**, [Reliant Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NRG_Stadium "NRG Stadium"), [Houston, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston "Houston") (hosts: [University of Houston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Houston "University of Houston"), [Rice University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rice_University "Rice University"))

**National semifinals and championship** (Final Four and championship)

*   April 3 and 5 
    *   [Lucas Oil Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucas_Oil_Stadium "Lucas Oil Stadium"), [Indianapolis, Indiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indianapolis "Indianapolis") (hosts: [Butler University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Butler_University "Butler University"), [Horizon League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horizon_League "Horizon League"))

Indianapolis hosted the Final Four for the 6th time, having previously hosted in [2006](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "2006 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament"), and was also the first to be held at the stadium; the [RCA Dome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RCA_Dome "RCA Dome") and [Market Square Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Market_Square_Arena "Market Square Arena") hosted past Final Fours when the event was held in Indianapolis.

## Game summaries

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010_NCAA_Division_I_men%27s_basketball_tournament&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Game summaries")]

### Midwest Region

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010_NCAA_Division_I_men%27s_basketball_tournament&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Midwest Region")]

#### First round

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010_NCAA_Division_I_men%27s_basketball_tournament&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: First round")]

The biggest upset of the first day came in [Providence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Providence,_Rhode_Island "Providence, Rhode Island"), Rhode Island, where 14th-seeded [Ohio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Ohio_Bobcats_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Ohio Bobcats men's basketball team") defeated third-seeded [Georgetown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Georgetown_Hoyas_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team") in convincing fashion, 97–83, for their first Tournament win since [1983](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1983_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "1983 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament"), when they ousted [Illinois State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois_State_Redbirds_men's_basketball "Illinois State Redbirds men's basketball") in the first round of that Tournament. [Armon Bassett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armon_Bassett "Armon Bassett") scored 32 points for the Bobcats, who shot 57 percent from the field and made 13 of 23 3-pointers.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-6) They advanced to face [Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Tennessee_Volunteers_basketball_team "2009–10 Tennessee Volunteers basketball team"), the sixth seed in the region. The Volunteers held off 11th seed [San Diego State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_San_Diego_State_Aztecs_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 San Diego State Aztecs men's basketball team"), 62–59, on head coach [Bruce Pearl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruce_Pearl "Bruce Pearl")'s 50th birthday. [J. P. Prince](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J._P._Prince "J. P. Prince") and Melvin Goins scored 15 points each for Tennessee.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-7)

In [Oklahoma City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oklahoma_City "Oklahoma City"), [Ali Farokhmanesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ali_Farokhmanesh "Ali Farokhmanesh") drilled a three-pointer with 4.9 seconds remaining to lift ninth-seeded [Northern Iowa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Northern_Iowa_Panthers_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Northern Iowa Panthers men's basketball team") over [UNLV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_UNLV_Runnin'_Rebels_basketball_team "2009–10 UNLV Runnin' Rebels basketball team"). It was the Panthers first Tournament win since [1990](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "1990 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-8) UNI advanced to face top-seeded [Kansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Kansas_Jayhawks_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team"). The top seed withheld an effort by [Lehigh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lehigh_Mountain_Hawks_men's_basketball "Lehigh Mountain Hawks men's basketball"), trailing the 16th seed early in the game and leading by just six at halftime before pulling away midway in the second half for a 90–74 win.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-9)

On the second day of play, 10th-seeded [Georgia Tech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Georgia_Tech_Yellow_Jackets_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball team") failed to make a single field goal in the final 8:19 of play, but sank 13 free throws to hold off No. 7 [Oklahoma State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Oklahoma_State_Cowboys_basketball_team "2009–10 Oklahoma State Cowboys basketball team"), 64–59, in [Milwaukee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milwaukee "Milwaukee"). [Gani Lawal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gani_Lawal "Gani Lawal") led Georgia Tech with 14 points.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-10) The Yellow Jackets advanced to play [Ohio State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Ohio_State_Buckeyes_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball team"), who defeated [UC Santa Barbara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_UC_Santa_Barbara_Gauchos_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 UC Santa Barbara Gauchos men's basketball team") 68–51. Buckeye star [Evan Turner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evan_Turner "Evan Turner") struggled from the field, shooting 2–13 and scoring nine points, and the Gauchos put up a fight, playing from behind most of the game.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-11)

Rounding out the Midwest bracket were [Maryland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Maryland_Terrapins_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Maryland Terrapins men's basketball team") and [Michigan State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Michigan_State_Spartans_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team") in [Spokane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spokane,_Washington "Spokane, Washington"), Washington. The Terrapins beat [Houston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston_Cougars_men's_basketball "Houston Cougars men's basketball") 89–77 behind a career-high 21 points and 17 rebounds from freshman Jordan Williams,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-12) while the Spartans edged [New Mexico State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_New_Mexico_State_Aggies_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 New Mexico State Aggies men's basketball team"), 70–67. The end of the game included a controversial lane violation call on Aggies player Troy Gillenwater with 18.6 seconds left that allowed MSU to reshoot a missed free throw and extend its lead to 3.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-13)

#### Second round

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2010_NCAA_Division_I_men%27s_basketball_tournament&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Second round")]

Northern Iowa stunned the nation by knocking off top overall seed Kansas, 69–67. Leading by just one in the final minute of play, Ali Farokhmanesh clinched the victory for the second time in as many games with a three-point basket that [ESPN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ESPN "ESPN")'s [Pat Forde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pat_Forde "Pat Forde") called "the greatest early-round shot in NCAA tournament history."[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-14) The win was significant for several reasons: it marked the Panthers' first trip ever to the Sweet Sixteen, and was the first time in six years a No. 1 seed was eliminated in the round of 32. It was also the first time since 1962 that a team from the [Missouri Valley Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri_Valley_Conference "Missouri Valley Conference") had defeated a top seed in the Tournament.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-15) Meanwhile, Michigan State lost guard [Kalin Lucas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalin_Lucas "Kalin Lucas") to a leg injury late in the first half of its game with Maryland. Michigan State extended its halftime lead of NINE to 16 in the second half before falling behind by one late after succumbing to Maryland's relentless pressure defense and some spectacular plays by [Greivis Vásquez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greivis_V%C3%A1squez "Greivis Vásquez"). But [Korie Lucious](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korie_Lucious "Korie Lucious") kept MSU from losing the game, hitting a 3-pointer as time ran out to lift his team past the Terrapins, 85–83.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-16) Lucas' injury proved to be a torn [Achilles tendon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Achilles_tendon "Achilles tendon"), putting the junior out of action for up to six months.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-17)

For the third time in four years, Tennessee made it to the regional semifinals with their 83–68 win over Ohio. J. P. Prince scored 18 points for the Volunteers, while [Scotty Hopson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scotty_Hopson "Scotty Hopson") added 17.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-18) In Milwaukee, Ohio State's [Evan Turner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evan_Turner "Evan Turner") bounced back from his off-night in the first round, nearly recording a triple-double (24 points, 9 rebounds and 9 assists) as the Buckeyes downed Georgia Tech 75–66.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-19)

**Devin Maurice Ebanks** (born October 28, 1989) is an American professional [basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball "Basketball") player for [Manama Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manama_Club_(basketball) "Manama Club (basketball)") of the [Bahraini Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bahraini_Premier_League_(basketball) "Bahraini Premier League (basketball)"). He was selected 43rd overall by the [Los Angeles Lakers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Lakers "Los Angeles Lakers") in the 2010 NBA draft, after playing [college basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_basketball "College basketball") for two seasons at [West Virginia University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Virginia_Mountaineers_men's_basketball "West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-1)

## High school career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Devin_Ebanks&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: High school career")]

As a sophomore at [Bishop Loughlin Memorial High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bishop_Loughlin_Memorial_High_School "Bishop Loughlin Memorial High School") in [Brooklyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn "Brooklyn"), New York, Ebanks averaged 18 points, six rebounds and 1.3 assists per game. In his junior season, at [St. Thomas More School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Thomas_More_School_(Connecticut) "St. Thomas More School (Connecticut)") in [Connecticut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connecticut "Connecticut"), he averaged 23 points, five rebounds, four assists and three steals. In his senior season, Ebanks recorded an average of 23 points, 10 rebounds and 5 assists per game. He scored over 1,000 points in his two seasons at St. Thomas More.

Ebanks received various honors while a prep player in high school. These honors included the [Jordan Brand Classic All-Star Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Jordan "Michael Jordan") in New York, playing [AAU](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amateur_Athletic_Union "Amateur Athletic Union") basketball, and being one of 30 players selected for the 2007 USA Basketball Development Festival at the [U.S. Olympic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympics "Olympics") Training Center in [Colorado Springs, Colorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs,_Colorado "Colorado Springs, Colorado"). While at the camp, Ebanks averaged 28.2 points and 4.8 rebounds per game.

Ebanks was widely regarded as one of the top high school players in the nation by scouting services, ranking 11th overall and 13th overall in the class by Rivals.com and Scout.com, respectively.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-2) He was being pursued by various colleges, such as [Indiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indiana_Hoosiers "Indiana Hoosiers"), [Memphis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memphis_Tigers "Memphis Tigers"), [Rutgers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rutgers_Scarlet_Knights "Rutgers Scarlet Knights") and [Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Longhorns "Texas Longhorns").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-3) Ebanks originally signed with the Indiana Hoosiers, but was released from his letter of intent after coach [Kelvin Sampson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kelvin_Sampson "Kelvin Sampson") was dismissed. Ebanks signed his letter of intent with [Bob Huggins'](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Huggins "Bob Huggins")[West Virginia University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Virginia_University "West Virginia University").

## College career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Devin_Ebanks&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: College career")]

At WVU, Ebanks totaled a then season-high 17 rebounds to go along with his 10 points, 3 assists, 3 steals and 2 blocks in a win over [Cleveland State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland_State_University "Cleveland State University").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-gamelog09-4) In the following 68–65 loss to #22 [Davidson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Davidson_University "Davidson University") in [Madison Square Garden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madison_Square_Garden "Madison Square Garden"), Ebanks led the team with 17 rebounds and also had 13 points.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-gamelog09-4) He then followed up in the [Duquesne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duquesne_University "Duquesne University") win with his third double-double: 15 points and 10 rebounds.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-gamelog09-4) However, his run was ended as he missed the majority of the Miami University victory with an injury.

Ebanks bounced back with 9 points and 10 rebounds in the win over [Radford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radford_University "Radford University"). In the 76–48 win over [Ohio State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ohio_State_Buckeyes "Ohio State Buckeyes"), Ebanks had 10 points and 5 rebounds. In the following win over [Seton Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seton_Hall "Seton Hall"), Ebanks had 10 points and 9 rebounds. He played 25 minutes of the loss to #1 [UConn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connecticut_Huskies "Connecticut Huskies"), however he only had 4 points and 2 rebounds; in the following loss to [Marquette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marquette_University "Marquette University") Ebanks had 8 points and 3 rebounds. In the win over [Marshall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marshall_Thundering_Herd "Marshall Thundering Herd"), he totaled 12 points and 4 rebounds, then 5 points and 10 rebounds in the win over [USF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Florida_Bulls "South Florida Bulls"). In the following win over [Georgetown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgetown_Hoyas "Georgetown Hoyas"), Ebanks had 9 points and 7 rebounds. In the loss to [Pittsburgh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh_Panthers "Pittsburgh Panthers") in the [Backyard Brawl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Backyard_Brawl "Backyard Brawl"), Ebanks had 9 points and 5 rebounds. In the following win over [St. John's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._John's_University_(New_York) "St. John's University (New York)"), he had 10 points and 8 rebounds.

In the 69–63 loss to [Louisville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisville_Cardinals "Louisville Cardinals"), Ebanks had 14 points and 6 rebounds. As the Mountaineers lost to [Syracuse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syracuse_Orangemen "Syracuse Orangemen"), he recorded 9 points and 9 rebounds. In the 86–59 win over [Providence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Providence_College "Providence College"), he had 13 points and 6 rebounds. In the second loss to Pittsburgh, he totaled a season-high 16 points with 7 rebounds. He followed the season-high point-performance with a double-double in the victory over [Villanova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villanova_University "Villanova University") – 16 points and 10 rebounds. In the 79–68 win over [Notre Dame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Notre_Dame_Fighting_Irish "Notre Dame Fighting Irish"), Ebanks recorded 11 points and 9 rebounds. In the following win over [Rutgers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rutgers_Scarlet_Knights "Rutgers Scarlet Knights"), Ebanks had another double-double with 14 points and 11 rebounds. Ebanks had a consecutive double-double in the loss to [Cincinnati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cincinnati_Bearcats "Cincinnati Bearcats") with 12 points and 14 rebounds. He then had 10 points and 7 rebounds in a victory over South Florida. Ebanks had his 9th double-double of his rookie campaign in the win over [DePaul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DePaul_University "DePaul University") with 14 points and 14 rebounds. Ebanks ended the regular season against #6 [Louisville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisville_Cardinals "Louisville Cardinals") with a season-high 16 points and 10 rebounds for his 10th double-double of the season. Following the 62–59 loss, Ebanks was named to the [Big East](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_East_Conference "Big East Conference") all-rookie team.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-5)

In the second round of the Big East Tournament against Notre Dame, Ebanks scored 7 points and had 5 assists to go with his season-high 18 rebounds. In the following round, defeating the #2 [Pittsburgh Panthers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh_Panthers "Pittsburgh Panthers") 74–60, he had a season-high 20 points with 7 rebounds and 3 assists. In the semifinals, he led the team to overtime against #20 [Syracuse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syracuse_Orangemen "Syracuse Orangemen"), setting a new career-high with 22 points and he also had 6 rebounds, 3 assists and 3 steals in the 74–69 loss. Ebanks was named to the first team All-Big East Tournament squad with his average of 16 points and 10 rebounds during the tenure. However, the Mountaineers lost in the first round of the [NCAA Tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NCAA_Men's_Division_I_Basketball_Championship "NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship") to [Dayton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Dayton "University of Dayton"), 68–60, with Ebanks scoring 14 points and grabbing 12 rebounds.

For his true freshman season, Ebanks averaged 10.5 points and 7.8 rebounds per game in his starting role. He had season-highs of 22 points against Syracuse and 18 rebounds against Notre Dame. He finished the year with double-point figures in 12 of his last 13 games with six double-doubles in those games.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-6) After some speculation, Ebanks announced he would return for his sophomore season.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-7)

## Professional career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Devin_Ebanks&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Professional career")]

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/68/Devin_Ebanks_in_2013.jpg/250px-Devin_Ebanks_in_2013.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Devin_Ebanks_in_2013.jpg)

Ebanks with the [Los Angeles Lakers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Lakers "Los Angeles Lakers") in 2013

Ebanks declared for the 2010 NBA draft, and was selected 43rd overall by the [Los Angeles Lakers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Lakers "Los Angeles Lakers"). He was signed on August 12, 2010. On December 27, 2010, the Los Angeles Lakers assigned Ebanks to the [Bakersfield Jam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bakersfield_Jam "Bakersfield Jam") of the NBA D-League. On January 8, 2011, the Lakers recalled Ebanks from the Jam as a result of an injury sustained by [Matt Barnes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Barnes "Matt Barnes").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-realgm-8) In February 2011, Ebanks fractured his leg while practicing before a game in Memphis.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-9)

On December 23, 2011, and in his sophomore season in the NBA, Ebanks was announced the starting small forward, in place of Matt Barnes, by new Laker coach [Mike Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Brown_(basketball,_born_1970) "Mike Brown (basketball, born 1970)").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-10) In his first game as a starter, Ebanks had 8 points, 1 rebound, and 2 assists, against the [Chicago Bulls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Bulls "Chicago Bulls").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-11) On February 15, 2012, he was assigned with the Los Angeles D-Fenders. He was later recalled on February 26, 2012.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-realgm-8) In his sophomore season, he averaged 4 points in 16.5 minutes per game. He also played 12 of 24 games as a starter.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-realgm-8)

On August 13, 2012, Ebanks re-signed with the Lakers to a one-year deal.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-12)

On September 13, 2013, Ebanks signed with the [Dallas Mavericks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas_Mavericks "Dallas Mavericks").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-13) However, he was waived on October 22.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-14) In November 2013, he was acquired by the [Texas Legends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Legends "Texas Legends").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-15) On February 3, 2014, Ebanks was named to the Prospects All-Star roster for the 2014 NBA D-League All-Star Game.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-16) On February 20, he was traded to the [Springfield Armor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Springfield_Armor "Springfield Armor").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-17)

In July 2014, he joined the NBA D-League Select Team for the [2014 NBA Summer League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_NBA_Summer_League "2014 NBA Summer League"). On August 28, 2014, he signed with [Bnei Herzliya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bnei_Herzliya "Bnei Herzliya") of Israel for the 2014–15 season.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-18) On October 28, 2014, he parted ways with Herzliya after just three games, with the team citing behavioral issues.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-19) On November 29, 2014, he signed with [Halcones Rojos Veracruz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halcones_Rojos_Veracruz "Halcones Rojos Veracruz") of Mexico for the rest of the season.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-20) In April 2015, he signed with [Brujos de Guayama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brujos_de_Guayama "Brujos de Guayama") of Puerto Rico for the rest of the 2015 [BSN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baloncesto_Superior_Nacional "Baloncesto Superior Nacional") season.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-21)

On October 31, 2015, Ebanks was acquired by the [Grand Rapids Drive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Rapids_Drive "Grand Rapids Drive") of the NBA Development League.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-22) On January 18, 2016, Ebanks scored 43 points in a 128–119 win over the [Maine Red Claws](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maine_Red_Claws "Maine Red Claws"), setting a new Drive franchise record.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-23) At the season's end, he was named to the All-NBA D-League Third Team.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-24)

On April 5, 2016, Ebanks signed with the [Leones de Ponce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leones_de_Ponce_(basketball) "Leones de Ponce (basketball)") of Puerto Rico for the rest of the 2016 [BSN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baloncesto_Superior_Nacional "Baloncesto Superior Nacional") season.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-25) Two days later, he made his debut for Leones in a 78–70 loss to the [Atenienses de Manatí](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atenienses_de_Manat%C3%AD_(basketball) "Atenienses de Manatí (basketball)"), recording 18 points, five rebounds and one assist in 34 minutes.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-26)

On August 18, 2016, Ebanks signed with [Reales de La Vega](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reales_de_La_Vega "Reales de La Vega") of Dominican Republic for the rest of the 2016 [LNB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liga_Nacional_de_Baloncesto "Liga Nacional de Baloncesto") season.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-27)

On August 1, 2017, Ebanks signed with Italian club [Mens Sana 1871 Basket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mens_Sana_1871_Basket "Mens Sana 1871 Basket") of the [Serie A2 Basket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serie_A2_Basket "Serie A2 Basket").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-28)

On October 10, 2020, [Indios de Mayagüez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indios_de_Mayag%C3%BCez_(basketball) "Indios de Mayagüez (basketball)") announced the signing of Ebanks.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-29)

On January 22, 2021, Greek club [Iraklis Thessaloniki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G.S._Iraklis_B.C. "G.S. Iraklis B.C.") announced the signing of Ebanks.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-30) On August 17, 2021, Ebanks signed with [Manama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manama_Club_(basketball) "Manama Club (basketball)") of the [Bahraini Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bahraini_Premier_League_(basketball) "Bahraini Premier League (basketball)").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-31) He helped Manama win their 21st national championship, as well as their 17th Bahraini Cup after he scored 34 points in the 103–97 finals win over [Al Hala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Hala_SC "Al-Hala SC").[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-32)
