**Devin Maurice Ebanks** (born October 28, 1989) is an American professional [basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball "Basketball") player for [Manama Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manama_Club_(basketball) "Manama Club (basketball)") of the [Bahraini Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bahraini_Premier_League_(basketball) "Bahraini Premier League (basketball)"). He was selected 43rd overall by the [Los Angeles Lakers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Lakers "Los Angeles Lakers") in the 2010 NBA draft, after playing [college basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_basketball "College basketball") for two seasons at [West Virginia University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Virginia_Mountaineers_men's_basketball "West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-1)

## High school career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Devin_Ebanks&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: High school career")]

As a sophomore at [Bishop Loughlin Memorial High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bishop_Loughlin_Memorial_High_School "Bishop Loughlin Memorial High School") in [Brooklyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn "Brooklyn"), New York, Ebanks averaged 18 points, six rebounds and 1.3 assists per game. In his junior season, at [St. Thomas More School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Thomas_More_School_(Connecticut) "St. Thomas More School (Connecticut)") in [Connecticut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connecticut "Connecticut"), he averaged 23 points, five rebounds, four assists and three steals. In his senior season, Ebanks recorded an average of 23 points, 10 rebounds and 5 assists per game. He scored over 1,000 points in his two seasons at St. Thomas More.

Ebanks received various honors while a prep player in high school. These honors included the [Jordan Brand Classic All-Star Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Jordan "Michael Jordan") in New York, playing [AAU](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amateur_Athletic_Union "Amateur Athletic Union") basketball, and being one of 30 players selected for the 2007 USA Basketball Development Festival at the [U.S. Olympic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympics "Olympics") Training Center in [Colorado Springs, Colorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs,_Colorado "Colorado Springs, Colorado"). While at the camp, Ebanks averaged 28.2 points and 4.8 rebounds per game.

Ebanks was widely regarded as one of the top high school players in the nation by scouting services, ranking 11th overall and 13th overall in the class by Rivals.com and Scout.com, respectively.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-2) He was being pursued by various colleges, such as [Indiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indiana_Hoosiers "Indiana Hoosiers"), [Memphis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memphis_Tigers "Memphis Tigers"), [Rutgers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rutgers_Scarlet_Knights "Rutgers Scarlet Knights") and [Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Longhorns "Texas Longhorns").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-3) Ebanks originally signed with the Indiana Hoosiers, but was released from his letter of intent after coach [Kelvin Sampson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kelvin_Sampson "Kelvin Sampson") was dismissed. Ebanks signed his letter of intent with [Bob Huggins'](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Huggins "Bob Huggins")[West Virginia University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Virginia_University "West Virginia University").

## College career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Devin_Ebanks&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: College career")]

At WVU, Ebanks totaled a then season-high 17 rebounds to go along with his 10 points, 3 assists, 3 steals and 2 blocks in a win over [Cleveland State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland_State_University "Cleveland State University").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-gamelog09-4) In the following 68–65 loss to #22 [Davidson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Davidson_University "Davidson University") in [Madison Square Garden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madison_Square_Garden "Madison Square Garden"), Ebanks led the team with 17 rebounds and also had 13 points.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-gamelog09-4) He then followed up in the [Duquesne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duquesne_University "Duquesne University") win with his third double-double: 15 points and 10 rebounds.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-gamelog09-4) However, his run was ended as he missed the majority of the Miami University victory with an injury.

Ebanks bounced back with 9 points and 10 rebounds in the win over [Radford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radford_University "Radford University"). In the 76–48 win over [Ohio State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ohio_State_Buckeyes "Ohio State Buckeyes"), Ebanks had 10 points and 5 rebounds. In the following win over [Seton Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seton_Hall "Seton Hall"), Ebanks had 10 points and 9 rebounds. He played 25 minutes of the loss to #1 [UConn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connecticut_Huskies "Connecticut Huskies"), however he only had 4 points and 2 rebounds; in the following loss to [Marquette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marquette_University "Marquette University") Ebanks had 8 points and 3 rebounds. In the win over [Marshall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marshall_Thundering_Herd "Marshall Thundering Herd"), he totaled 12 points and 4 rebounds, then 5 points and 10 rebounds in the win over [USF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Florida_Bulls "South Florida Bulls"). In the following win over [Georgetown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgetown_Hoyas "Georgetown Hoyas"), Ebanks had 9 points and 7 rebounds. In the loss to [Pittsburgh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh_Panthers "Pittsburgh Panthers") in the [Backyard Brawl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Backyard_Brawl "Backyard Brawl"), Ebanks had 9 points and 5 rebounds. In the following win over [St. John's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._John's_University_(New_York) "St. John's University (New York)"), he had 10 points and 8 rebounds.

In the 69–63 loss to [Louisville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisville_Cardinals "Louisville Cardinals"), Ebanks had 14 points and 6 rebounds. As the Mountaineers lost to [Syracuse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syracuse_Orangemen "Syracuse Orangemen"), he recorded 9 points and 9 rebounds. In the 86–59 win over [Providence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Providence_College "Providence College"), he had 13 points and 6 rebounds. In the second loss to Pittsburgh, he totaled a season-high 16 points with 7 rebounds. He followed the season-high point-performance with a double-double in the victory over [Villanova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villanova_University "Villanova University") – 16 points and 10 rebounds. In the 79–68 win over [Notre Dame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Notre_Dame_Fighting_Irish "Notre Dame Fighting Irish"), Ebanks recorded 11 points and 9 rebounds. In the following win over [Rutgers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rutgers_Scarlet_Knights "Rutgers Scarlet Knights"), Ebanks had another double-double with 14 points and 11 rebounds. Ebanks had a consecutive double-double in the loss to [Cincinnati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cincinnati_Bearcats "Cincinnati Bearcats") with 12 points and 14 rebounds. He then had 10 points and 7 rebounds in a victory over South Florida. Ebanks had his 9th double-double of his rookie campaign in the win over [DePaul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DePaul_University "DePaul University") with 14 points and 14 rebounds. Ebanks ended the regular season against #6 [Louisville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisville_Cardinals "Louisville Cardinals") with a season-high 16 points and 10 rebounds for his 10th double-double of the season. Following the 62–59 loss, Ebanks was named to the [Big East](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_East_Conference "Big East Conference") all-rookie team.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-5)

In the second round of the Big East Tournament against Notre Dame, Ebanks scored 7 points and had 5 assists to go with his season-high 18 rebounds. In the following round, defeating the #2 [Pittsburgh Panthers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh_Panthers "Pittsburgh Panthers") 74–60, he had a season-high 20 points with 7 rebounds and 3 assists. In the semifinals, he led the team to overtime against #20 [Syracuse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syracuse_Orangemen "Syracuse Orangemen"), setting a new career-high with 22 points and he also had 6 rebounds, 3 assists and 3 steals in the 74–69 loss. Ebanks was named to the first team All-Big East Tournament squad with his average of 16 points and 10 rebounds during the tenure. However, the Mountaineers lost in the first round of the [NCAA Tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NCAA_Men's_Division_I_Basketball_Championship "NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship") to [Dayton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Dayton "University of Dayton"), 68–60, with Ebanks scoring 14 points and grabbing 12 rebounds.

For his true freshman season, Ebanks averaged 10.5 points and 7.8 rebounds per game in his starting role. He had season-highs of 22 points against Syracuse and 18 rebounds against Notre Dame. He finished the year with double-point figures in 12 of his last 13 games with six double-doubles in those games.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-6) After some speculation, Ebanks announced he would return for his sophomore season.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-7)

## Professional career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Devin_Ebanks&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Professional career")]

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/68/Devin_Ebanks_in_2013.jpg/250px-Devin_Ebanks_in_2013.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Devin_Ebanks_in_2013.jpg)

Ebanks with the [Los Angeles Lakers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Lakers "Los Angeles Lakers") in 2013

Ebanks declared for the 2010 NBA draft, and was selected 43rd overall by the [Los Angeles Lakers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Lakers "Los Angeles Lakers"). He was signed on August 12, 2010. On December 27, 2010, the Los Angeles Lakers assigned Ebanks to the [Bakersfield Jam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bakersfield_Jam "Bakersfield Jam") of the NBA D-League. On January 8, 2011, the Lakers recalled Ebanks from the Jam as a result of an injury sustained by [Matt Barnes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Barnes "Matt Barnes").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-realgm-8) In February 2011, Ebanks fractured his leg while practicing before a game in Memphis.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-9)

On December 23, 2011, and in his sophomore season in the NBA, Ebanks was announced the starting small forward, in place of Matt Barnes, by new Laker coach [Mike Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Brown_(basketball,_born_1970) "Mike Brown (basketball, born 1970)").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-10) In his first game as a starter, Ebanks had 8 points, 1 rebound, and 2 assists, against the [Chicago Bulls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Bulls "Chicago Bulls").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-11) On February 15, 2012, he was assigned with the Los Angeles D-Fenders. He was later recalled on February 26, 2012.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-realgm-8) In his sophomore season, he averaged 4 points in 16.5 minutes per game. He also played 12 of 24 games as a starter.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-realgm-8)

On August 13, 2012, Ebanks re-signed with the Lakers to a one-year deal.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-12)

On September 13, 2013, Ebanks signed with the [Dallas Mavericks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas_Mavericks "Dallas Mavericks").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-13) However, he was waived on October 22.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-14) In November 2013, he was acquired by the [Texas Legends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Legends "Texas Legends").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-15) On February 3, 2014, Ebanks was named to the Prospects All-Star roster for the 2014 NBA D-League All-Star Game.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-16) On February 20, he was traded to the [Springfield Armor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Springfield_Armor "Springfield Armor").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-17)

In July 2014, he joined the NBA D-League Select Team for the [2014 NBA Summer League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_NBA_Summer_League "2014 NBA Summer League"). On August 28, 2014, he signed with [Bnei Herzliya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bnei_Herzliya "Bnei Herzliya") of Israel for the 2014–15 season.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-18) On October 28, 2014, he parted ways with Herzliya after just three games, with the team citing behavioral issues.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-19) On November 29, 2014, he signed with [Halcones Rojos Veracruz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halcones_Rojos_Veracruz "Halcones Rojos Veracruz") of Mexico for the rest of the season.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-20) In April 2015, he signed with [Brujos de Guayama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brujos_de_Guayama "Brujos de Guayama") of Puerto Rico for the rest of the 2015 [BSN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baloncesto_Superior_Nacional "Baloncesto Superior Nacional") season.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-21)

On October 31, 2015, Ebanks was acquired by the [Grand Rapids Drive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Rapids_Drive "Grand Rapids Drive") of the NBA Development League.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-22) On January 18, 2016, Ebanks scored 43 points in a 128–119 win over the [Maine Red Claws](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maine_Red_Claws "Maine Red Claws"), setting a new Drive franchise record.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-23) At the season's end, he was named to the All-NBA D-League Third Team.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-24)

On April 5, 2016, Ebanks signed with the [Leones de Ponce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leones_de_Ponce_(basketball) "Leones de Ponce (basketball)") of Puerto Rico for the rest of the 2016 [BSN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baloncesto_Superior_Nacional "Baloncesto Superior Nacional") season.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-25) Two days later, he made his debut for Leones in a 78–70 loss to the [Atenienses de Manatí](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atenienses_de_Manat%C3%AD_(basketball) "Atenienses de Manatí (basketball)"), recording 18 points, five rebounds and one assist in 34 minutes.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-26)

On August 18, 2016, Ebanks signed with [Reales de La Vega](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reales_de_La_Vega "Reales de La Vega") of Dominican Republic for the rest of the 2016 [LNB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liga_Nacional_de_Baloncesto "Liga Nacional de Baloncesto") season.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-27)

On August 1, 2017, Ebanks signed with Italian club [Mens Sana 1871 Basket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mens_Sana_1871_Basket "Mens Sana 1871 Basket") of the [Serie A2 Basket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serie_A2_Basket "Serie A2 Basket").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-28)

On October 10, 2020, [Indios de Mayagüez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indios_de_Mayag%C3%BCez_(basketball) "Indios de Mayagüez (basketball)") announced the signing of Ebanks.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-29)

On January 22, 2021, Greek club [Iraklis Thessaloniki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G.S._Iraklis_B.C. "G.S. Iraklis B.C.") announced the signing of Ebanks.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-30) On August 17, 2021, Ebanks signed with [Manama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manama_Club_(basketball) "Manama Club (basketball)") of the [Bahraini Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bahraini_Premier_League_(basketball) "Bahraini Premier League (basketball)").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-31) He helped Manama win their 21st national championship, as well as their 17th Bahraini Cup after he scored 34 points in the 103–97 finals win over [Al Hala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Hala_SC "Al-Hala SC").[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Ebanks#cite_note-32)

**Da'Sean Butler** (born January 25, 1988) is an American professional [basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball "Basketball") coach and former player who is a player enhancement coach for the [Boston Celtics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston_Celtics "Boston Celtics") of the [National Basketball Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Basketball_Association "National Basketball Association") (NBA). He played [college basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_basketball "College basketball") for [West Virginia University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Virginia_Mountaineers_men's_basketball "West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball"). Butler was drafted 42nd overall by the [Miami Heat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_Heat "Miami Heat") in the 2010 NBA draft.

## College career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Da%27Sean_Butler&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: College career")]

### Freshman season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Da%27Sean_Butler&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Freshman season")]

Butler scored a career high 21 points in a game against Seton Hall. Against [Slippery Rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slippery_Rock_University_of_Pennsylvania "Slippery Rock University of Pennsylvania"), Butler had 15 points and nine rebounds off the bench, then had eight points against [Arkansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Arkansas "University of Arkansas"). He had 9 points against [North Carolina State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Carolina_State "North Carolina State"), then 10 points and six rebounds against [Duquesne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duquesne_University "Duquesne University"). Butler scored 14 points against [The Citadel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Citadel_(military_college) "The Citadel (military college)"), 16 points against [UConn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UConn "UConn"), 7 points against [Villanova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villanova_University "Villanova University"), and then six points against [St. John's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._John's_University_(New_York) "St. John's University (New York)"). He then scored 9 points and a season-high 10 rebounds against [Notre Dame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Notre_Dame "University of Notre Dame"), followed by 12 points and six rebounds against [South Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_South_Florida "University of South Florida"). Butler then had 14 points and 8 rebounds against [Cincinnati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Cincinnati "University of Cincinnati"), 17 points against [Rutgers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rutgers "Rutgers"), and a team-high 14 points against [Pittsburgh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Pittsburgh "University of Pittsburgh") in the [Backyard Brawl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Backyard_Brawl "Backyard Brawl"). In the huge upset win over [UCLA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UCLA "UCLA"), Butler had 13 points, while scoring 17 points against [Louisville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Louisville "University of Louisville") in the [Big East tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_East_Conference_Men's_Basketball_Player_of_the_Year "Big East Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year"). The Mountaineers eventually made it in the [NIT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Invitation_Tournament "National Invitation Tournament") Tournament, and all the way to the finals. In the finals win against [Clemson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clemson_University "Clemson University"), Butler had 20 points, as the Mountaineers were named NIT champions.

Butler was named to the [Big East](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_East_Conference "Big East Conference") all-freshman team, while leading the Mountaineers to an NIT Championship. Butler averaged 10.1 points per game, averaging 23.3 minutes per game off the bench, while also averaging 3.5 rebounds per game.

### Sophomore season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Da%27Sean_Butler&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Sophomore season")]

After the 2007 NIT Championship win, Mountaineers head coach [John Beilein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Beilein "John Beilein") announced he would be leaving [West Virginia University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Virginia_University "West Virginia University") to take the head coaching position at the [University of Michigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Michigan "University of Michigan"). Soon after, former head coach of [Kansas State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_State_University "Kansas State University")'s basketball team and West Virginia alumnus [Bob Huggins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Huggins "Bob Huggins") announced he accepted an offer to coach at West Virginia.

In the season-opening exhibition game against [Mountain State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mountain_State_University "Mountain State University"), Butler earned his first career start as the Mountaineers won 88–65. Butler scored 16 points and added 8 rebounds and three assists as he and fellow guard [Darris Nichols](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darris_Nichols "Darris Nichols") both went into double-digits in points. In the season-opener against [Arkansas-Monticello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Arkansas_at_Monticello "University of Arkansas at Monticello"), Butler scored 14 points while also grabbing a season-high 9 rebounds. In the 72–74 loss to [Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Tennessee "University of Tennessee"), Butler happened to score 16 points and grab 7 rebounds, while he scored 13 in the victories over New Mexico State and [Auburn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auburn_University "Auburn University"). Butler scored a season-high 18 points against [Duquesne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duquesne_University "Duquesne University"), while also grabbing 8 rebounds. He then scored 14 points against Maryland County, grabbing 9 rebounds, and [Radford University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radford_University "Radford University"), and then scored 10 against [Canisius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canisius_College "Canisius College").

In the 88–82 loss to [Oklahoma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Oklahoma "University of Oklahoma"), Butler scored 15 points and grabbed 5 rebounds. In the loss to [Notre Dame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Notre_Dame "University of Notre Dame"), Butler only scored 8 points but did grab 5 rebounds. Then in the victory over [Marquette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marquette_University "Marquette University"), Butler scored 13 points with 5 rebounds, but in the loss to [Louisville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Louisville "University of Louisville") he only scored 8 again. In the victory over [Syracuse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syracuse_University "Syracuse University"), Butler grabbed 6 rebounds to go along with his 13 points. Butler was key in the [St. John's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._John's_University_(New_York) "St. John's University (New York)") victory with 19 points and 9 rebounds. Butler recorded his first double-double of the season in the loss to [USF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_South_Florida "University of South Florida"), with 15 points and 12 rebounds. In the 66–64 victory over [Marshall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marshall_University "Marshall University"), Butler scored 18 points – including the game-winning shot in the lane with 6 seconds left.

Then in the 58–57 loss to No. 9 [Georgetown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgetown_University "Georgetown University"), Butler attempted to score the game-winning points again. However, his layup attempt was blocked by [Patrick Ewing Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_Ewing_Jr. "Patrick Ewing Jr.") The call was questionable however, as many believe it was actually a [goaltending](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goaltending "Goaltending") which would result in the points being rewarded and the Mountaineer-victory.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-1) However, Butler finished with 12 points and 4 rebounds. In an 81–63 victory over [Rutgers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rutgers "Rutgers"), Butler scored 12 points. He then followed that game with 15 points and 8 rebounds against [Seton Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seton_Hall "Seton Hall"). In the 78–56 loss to [Villanova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villanova_University "Villanova University"), Butler scored 10 points and grabbed 7 rebounds. In the 80–53 victory over [Providence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Providence_College "Providence College"), Butler scored 13 points and grabbed 4 rebounds.

In the 85–73 victory over [DePaul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DePaul_University "DePaul University") to gain the 20th win of the season, Butler scored 14 points and grabbed 13 rebounds for his second double-double of the season. In the 79–71 loss to the [Connecticut Huskies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connecticut_Huskies_men's_basketball "Connecticut Huskies men's basketball"), Butler scored 9 points and added 7 rebounds. In the home finale victory over the [Pittsburgh Panthers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh_Panthers "Pittsburgh Panthers"), 76–62, Butler scored 10 points and grabbed 6 rebounds. In the regular season finale, an 83–74 overtime victory over Providence, Butler scored 18 points, grabbed 10 rebounds, and dished 5 assists to finish the regular season. He finished the season with 12.5 points and 6.1 rebounds per game.

In the 58–53 victory over Providence to open the Big East tournament, Butler scored 17 points and added 9 rebounds. In the second round of the tourney, the Mountaineers upset #15-ranked Connecticut, 78–72. Butler contributed with 17 points and a team-high 9 rebounds. However, as the Mountaineers lost 55–72 in the semifinal matchup against the #8 [Georgetown Hoyas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgetown_Hoyas "Georgetown Hoyas"), Butler scored 16 points with 3 rebounds and assists.

In the first round of the [NCAA tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_NCAA_Men's_Division_I_Basketball_Tournament "2008 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament"), Butler scored 19 points with 7 rebounds as the No. 7-seed Mountaineers defeated the #10-seed [Arizona Wildcats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arizona_Wildcats "Arizona Wildcats"). In the second round, the Mountaineers upset the #2-seed [Duke Blue Devils](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duke_Blue_Devils "Duke Blue Devils") 73–67, with Butler scoring 8 points and grabbing 5 rebounds. Then, in the Sweet 16 loss in overtime to No. 3-seed [Xavier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xavier_Musketeers_men's_basketball "Xavier Musketeers men's basketball"), Butler scored 16 points and grabbed 7 rebounds.

Butler finished his sophomore season by averaging 12.9 points and 6.2 rebounds per game. During the Mountaineers Sweet 16 NCAA Tournament run, Butler averaged 14.3 points and 6.3 rebounds per game.

### Junior season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Da%27Sean_Butler&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Junior season")]

Butler began his junior season under returning head coach [Bob Huggins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Huggins "Bob Huggins") in the 98–78 exhibition win over [Mountain State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mountain_State_University "Mountain State University"). In the victory, Butler led the Mountaineers with 38 points and 11 rebounds. In the regular season opener against [Elon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elon_University "Elon University"), Butler scored 19 points and totaled 6 rebounds and steals. Against [Longwood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Longwood_University "Longwood University"), he then totaled 12 points and 4 rebounds. Opening the Las Vegas Invitational Tournament, the Mountaineers defeated [Delaware State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delaware_State "Delaware State"), with Butler scoring 12 points and grabbing 7 rebounds. He then scored 12 against [Iowa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iowa_Hawkeyes "Iowa Hawkeyes"), and before scoring 7 points with 9 boards in the loss to [Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kentucky_Wildcats "Kentucky Wildcats"). However, the Mountaineers then defeated [Mississippi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ole_Miss "Ole Miss"), with Butler scoring 22 points and grabbing 10 rebounds – his first double-double of the season. As the Mountaineers then beat [Cleveland State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland_State "Cleveland State"), Butler led the team with 18 points. In the 68–65 last-second loss to No. 22 [Davidson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Davidson_University "Davidson University") and [Stephen Curry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Curry "Stephen Curry") in [Madison Square Garden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madison_Square_Garden "Madison Square Garden"), Butler led the Mountaineers with 24 points and 14 rebounds – his second double-double in three games. Butler reached his 1,000 career points during the Miami University victory, in which he scored a career-high 28 points out of the team's 82–46 victory and also had 5 rebounds. Most Rebounds in his Career.

Butler then had 11 points against [Radford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radford_University "Radford University"), followed by 16 points and 6 rebounds in the 76–48 victory over #13 [Ohio State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ohio_State_Buckeyes "Ohio State Buckeyes"). In the 92–66 win over [Seton Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seton_Hall "Seton Hall"), Butler had 18 points, 9 rebounds and 5 assists. In the next loss to No. 5 [UConn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connecticut_Huskies "Connecticut Huskies"), 61–55, Butler scored 13 points and had 5 steals. As the Mountaineers then lost to No. 15 [Marquette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marquette_Golden_Eagles "Marquette Golden Eagles"), Butler scored 16 points and had 5 rebounds. Butler then had 17 points and 7 rebounds in the victory over [Marshall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marshall_University "Marshall University"). Against [South Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Florida_Bulls "South Florida Bulls"), Butler scored 27 points with 4 rebounds, and then he totaled 27 points and 8 rebounds in the win over #14 [Georgetown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgetown_Hoyas "Georgetown Hoyas"). In the following loss to No. 4 [Pittsburgh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh_Panthers "Pittsburgh Panthers"), Butler scored 21 points and had 6 rebounds. In the win over [St. John's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._John's_University_(New_York) "St. John's University (New York)"), Butler scored 21 points and had 7 rebounds. Butler recorded his fifth-consecutive 20-point game with 23 points against #7 [Louisville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisville_Cardinals "Louisville Cardinals") to go with 8 rebounds. Butler followed the Louisville loss with 23 points, 4 rebounds, 4 assists, and 4 steals against [Syracuse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syracuse_Orangemen "Syracuse Orangemen"). Butler's consecutive 20-point game streak ended at six games against [Providence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Providence_College "Providence College") with his 17 points and 9 rebounds in the 86–59 victory. In the [Backyard Brawl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Backyard_Brawl "Backyard Brawl") loss to No. 4 [Pittsburgh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh_Panthers "Pittsburgh Panthers"), Butler only scored 4 points in limited playing time due to foul trouble.

On February 13, the Mountaineers defeated #13 [Villanova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villanova_University "Villanova University") 93–72. In the victory, Butler scored a career-high 43 points; 24 points coming in the first-half. Butler's point total was the second-highest individual scoring performance in a Big East conference game since the 2002–03 season, only one-point shy of [Marcus Hatten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcus_Hatten "Marcus Hatten")'s 44 point performance in 2003.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-2) His 43 points were the third-most ever scored in the [WVU Coliseum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WVU_Coliseum "WVU Coliseum"), the most by a WVU player in conference play ever and the first 40-point performance since Lowes Moore in 1978.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-3) In the following 79–68 win over [Notre Dame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Notre_Dame_Fighting_Irish "Notre Dame Fighting Irish"), Butler had 19 points, 4 rebounds and 4 assists. He followed with 12 points and 4 assists in the win over [Rutgers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rutgers_Scarlet_Knights "Rutgers Scarlet Knights"). In the 65–61 loss to [Cincinnati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cincinnati_Bearcats "Cincinnati Bearcats"), Butler had 8 points and 4 assists. He then had 9 points and 12 rebounds in a win over [USF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Florida_Bulls "South Florida Bulls"). Butler then had a double-double in the win over [DePaul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DePaul_University "DePaul University") with 16 points and 10 rebounds. In the regular season finale against #6 [Louisville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisville_Cardinals "Louisville Cardinals"), Butler scored 10 points with 10 rebounds for a second-straight double-double. Following the 62–59 loss, he was named to the All-Big East second team.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-4)

In the second round of the Big East tournament against Notre Dame, Butler scored 20 points and grabbed 5 rebounds. In the quarterfinals' 74–60 win over #2 [Pittsburgh Panthers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh_Panthers "Pittsburgh Panthers"), Butler scored 16 points with 4 assists and 3 rebounds despite sitting out due to 4 personal fouls. In the semifinal round, a 74–69 loss to No. 20 [Syracuse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syracuse_Orangemen "Syracuse Orangemen"), Butler scored 21 points and had 6 rebounds. In the Big East tournament, Butler averaged 19 points and 4.6 rebounds. However, the Mountaineers were upset in the first round of the [NCAA tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NCAA_Men's_Division_I_Basketball_Championship "NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship") by [Dayton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Dayton "University of Dayton"), 68–60, with Butler scoring 12 points and grabbing 5 rebounds.

Butler finished his junior season with an average of 19.1 points per game and 5.9 rebounds per game. Butler had a season-high 43 points against Villanova and a season-high 14 rebounds against Davidson. Butler scored 20 or more points 12 times in the campaign.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-5)

### Senior season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Da%27Sean_Butler&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Senior season")]

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/41/Da%27Sean_Butler_2010_NCAA_West_Virginia_Elite_Eight.jpg/250px-Da%27Sean_Butler_2010_NCAA_West_Virginia_Elite_Eight.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Da'Sean_Butler_2010_NCAA_West_Virginia_Elite_Eight.jpg)

De'Sean Butler of West Virginia University lifts the East Region trophy after defeating Kentucky 73–66 in the 2010 NCAA men's basketball tournament.

Butler was invited to the 2009 USA Basketball Men's World University Games Team training camp prior to his senior season.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-6) Butler and the Top10-ranked Mountaineers opened up the season with a win over Loyola-Maryland, in which Butler recorded 26 points and 7 rebounds. In a later win over Portland, Butler scored 26 points with 6 rebounds. At the end of December, Butler hit a game-winning jumper to defeat Marquette, adding to his 17 total points.

After losing three games in early to mid-January, Butler and the Mountaineers bounced back with a win over #25 Ohio State and then a win over Louisville in which Butler scored 27 points. In a following win over St. John's, Butler scored 33 points, then he added 32 points in a triple overtime loss to No. 23 Pittsburgh. The Mountaineers ended their regular season with a 68–66 victory over #6 Villanova in which Butler had a double-double: 21 points and 10 rebounds.

In the Mountaineers' opening game of the Big East tournament, West Virginia defeated Cincinnati with help from Butler, who banked in the game-winning three-pointer with no time left to win 54–51. In the following 53–51 victory over [Notre Dame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Notre_Dame_Fighting_Irish "Notre Dame Fighting Irish") in the semifinals, Butler scored 24 points. In the championship game, Butler again led the Mountaineers to victory with the game-winning bucket over #22 Georgetown. The victory was the first ever Big East title for the Mountaineers.

Entering the NCAA Tournament as a two-seed, the Mountaineers handled Morgan State in the opening round. Butler scored 28 points and added 8 rebounds in the second round victory over Missouri. After defeating Washington in the Sweet 16, the Mountaineers upset the 1-seed and tourney favorite Kentucky Wildcats 73–66, to advance to the school's second Final Four appearance. Butler had 18 points in the Elite Eight victory, including finishing 4–8 from the 3-point line.

Butler and Duke's [Jon Scheyer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Scheyer "Jon Scheyer") were the only finalists in 2010's [Final Four](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Final_Four "Final Four") for the [Lowe's Senior CLASS Award for Men's Basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lowe's_Senior_CLASS_Award "Lowe's Senior CLASS Award"),[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-7) which on April 3, 2010, was awarded to Butler. Later that day, in the second half of the Final Four loss to the [Duke Blue Devils](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Duke_Blue_Devils_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team"), Butler injured his left knee. Butler tore his ACL, sprained his MCL and sustained two bone bruises.

Butler was one of 10 finalists for the 2010 [John R. Wooden Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_R._Wooden_Award "John R. Wooden Award").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-autogenerated4-8) It is given to the National Player of the Year in college basketball by The [Los Angeles Athletic Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Athletic_Club "Los Angeles Athletic Club").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-9)

## Professional career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Da%27Sean_Butler&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Professional career")]

### Austin Toros (2011)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Da%27Sean_Butler&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Austin Toros (2011)")]

After months of rehabilitation, Butler was selected by the Miami Heat 42nd overall in the 2010 NBA draft. Butler signed with the Heat on August 30, 2010.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-10) However, on October 25, Butler was waived by the Heat at the end of training camp.

On March 25, 2011, Butler signed a contract with the [San Antonio Spurs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Antonio_Spurs "San Antonio Spurs") and was assigned to the [Austin Toros](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austin_Spurs "Austin Spurs") of the [NBA Development League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_G_League "NBA G League").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-11)

### VEF Rīga (2011)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Da%27Sean_Butler&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: VEF Rīga (2011)")]

In November 2011 he joined [Latvian Basketball League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latvijas_Basketbola_l%C4%ABga "Latvijas Basketbola līga") club [VEF Rīga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BC_VEF_R%C4%ABga "BC VEF Rīga") during the [2011 NBA Lockout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_NBA_Lockout "2011 NBA Lockout").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-VEF-12)

### Return to Austin Toros (2011–2012)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Da%27Sean_Butler&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Return to Austin Toros (2011–2012)")]

Butler returned soon after to the San Antonio Spurs in time for the start of the 2011–2012 NBA season. He was officially waived by the Spurs on December 13, 2011.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-13)

He re-signed with the [Austin Toros](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austin_Spurs "Austin Spurs") during 2012, but was released towards the end of the season after requiring additional surgeries on the same knee.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-14)

### Okapi Aalstar (2013–2014)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Da%27Sean_Butler&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Okapi Aalstar (2013–2014)")]

On August 2, 2013, he signed with the Belgian team [Okapi Aalstar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Okapi_Aalstar "Okapi Aalstar") for the 2013–14 season.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-15) On April 30, 2014, Butler recorded a career-high 31 points, shooting 13-of-19 from the field, along with five rebounds, two assists and two steals in a 110–98 win over [Excelsior Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Excelsior_Brussels "Excelsior Brussels").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-16)

Butler won the [2013 Belgian Supercup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgian_Basketball_Supercup "Belgian Basketball Supercup") with Okapi Aalstar. In 48 games played during the 2013–14 season, he averaged 16.2 points, 4.2 rebounds, 1.2 assists and 1.2 steals per game. On June 15, 2014, Butler was named the Belgian League Forward of the Year and earned a spot in the All-Belgian League Second Team.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-17)

### Châlons Reims (2014–2015)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Da%27Sean_Butler&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Châlons Reims (2014–2015)")]

On June 22, 2014, he signed a one-year deal with the French team [Châlons Reims](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champagne_Ch%C3%A2lons_Reims_Basket "Champagne Châlons Reims Basket").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-18) On May 9, 2015, Butler recorded a season-high 24 points, shooting 9-of-13 from the field, along with four rebounds and three assists in an 85–75 win over [Pau-Orthez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%89lan_B%C3%A9arnais_Pau-Lacq-Orthez "Élan Béarnais Pau-Lacq-Orthez").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-19)

### ratiopharm Ulm (2015–2018)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Da%27Sean_Butler&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: ratiopharm Ulm (2015–2018)")]

On July 12, 2015, he signed with the German team [ratiopharm Ulm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ratiopharm_Ulm "Ratiopharm Ulm") for the 2014–15 season.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-20) On April 16, 2016, Butler recorded a season-high 27 points, shooting 7-of-10 from 3-point range, along with five rebounds, two assists and two steals in an 87–71 win over [Giessen 46ers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giessen_46ers "Giessen 46ers").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-21) Butler helped Ulm reach the [2016 BBL Finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_BBL_Playoffs "2016 BBL Playoffs"), where they eventually lost to [Brose Bamberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brose_Bamberg "Brose Bamberg").

On May 24, 2016, he re-signed with Ulm for the 2016–17 season.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-22) Butler helped Ulm reach the [2017 BBL Playoffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_BBL_Playoffs "2017 BBL Playoffs") as the first seed, but they eventually were eliminated by [EWE Baskets Oldenburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EWE_Baskets_Oldenburg "EWE Baskets Oldenburg") in the Semifinals.

On June 17, 2017, he signed a one-year contract extension with Ulm.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-23) In 23 BBL games played during the 2017–18 season, he averaged 10.3 points, 4.5 rebounds and 1.0 steals per game, shooting 39.6 percent from 3-point range.

### Hapoel Jerusalem (2018–2019)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Da%27Sean_Butler&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Hapoel Jerusalem (2018–2019)")]

On August 12, 2018, he signed a two-year deal with the Israeli team [Hapoel Jerusalem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hapoel_Jerusalem_B.C. "Hapoel Jerusalem B.C.").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-24) Butler won the [2019 Israeli State Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Israeli_Basketball_State_Cup "2018–19 Israeli Basketball State Cup") with Jerusalem.

### Hapoel Be'er Sheva (2019–2020)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Da%27Sean_Butler&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Hapoel Be'er Sheva (2019–2020)")]

On October 2, 2019, he signed with [Hapoel Be'er Sheva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hapoel_Be'er_Sheva_B.C. "Hapoel Be'er Sheva B.C.") for the 2019–20 season.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-25) On December 22, 2019, Butler recorded a season-high 25 points, including a three-pointer at the buzzer to give Be'er Sheva a 79–77 win over [Maccabi Ashdod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maccabi_Ashdod_B.C. "Maccabi Ashdod B.C.").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-26)

## Coaching career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Da%27Sean_Butler&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Coaching career")]

In February 2021, Butler joined [Wheeling University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wheeling_Cardinals "Wheeling Cardinals") as an assistant coach. He had been friends with the head coach Chris Richardson since he was 18 years old, and Richardson invited him to join his staff. In October 2021, Butler was hired as an assistant at the [College Park Skyhawks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_Park_Skyhawks "College Park Skyhawks") of the [NBA G League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_G_League "NBA G League").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-27)

In July 2023, Butler returned to his alma mater, [West Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Virginia_Mountaineers_men's_basketball "West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball"), as an assistant coach under [Josh Eilert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josh_Eilert "Josh Eilert").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-28)

In July 2024, Butler joined [Boston Celtics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston_Celtics "Boston Celtics") as a player enhancement coach under [Joe Mazzulla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla "Joe Mazzulla").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-29)

**Da'Sean Butler** (born January 25, 1988) is an American professional [basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball "Basketball") coach and former player who is a player enhancement coach for the [Boston Celtics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston_Celtics "Boston Celtics") of the [National Basketball Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Basketball_Association "National Basketball Association") (NBA). He played [college basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_basketball "College basketball") for [West Virginia University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Virginia_Mountaineers_men's_basketball "West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball"). Butler was drafted 42nd overall by the [Miami Heat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_Heat "Miami Heat") in the 2010 NBA draft.

## College career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Da%27Sean_Butler&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: College career")]

### Freshman season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Da%27Sean_Butler&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Freshman season")]

Butler scored a career high 21 points in a game against Seton Hall. Against [Slippery Rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slippery_Rock_University_of_Pennsylvania "Slippery Rock University of Pennsylvania"), Butler had 15 points and nine rebounds off the bench, then had eight points against [Arkansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Arkansas "University of Arkansas"). He had 9 points against [North Carolina State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Carolina_State "North Carolina State"), then 10 points and six rebounds against [Duquesne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duquesne_University "Duquesne University"). Butler scored 14 points against [The Citadel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Citadel_(military_college) "The Citadel (military college)"), 16 points against [UConn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UConn "UConn"), 7 points against [Villanova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villanova_University "Villanova University"), and then six points against [St. John's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._John's_University_(New_York) "St. John's University (New York)"). He then scored 9 points and a season-high 10 rebounds against [Notre Dame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Notre_Dame "University of Notre Dame"), followed by 12 points and six rebounds against [South Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_South_Florida "University of South Florida"). Butler then had 14 points and 8 rebounds against [Cincinnati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Cincinnati "University of Cincinnati"), 17 points against [Rutgers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rutgers "Rutgers"), and a team-high 14 points against [Pittsburgh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Pittsburgh "University of Pittsburgh") in the [Backyard Brawl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Backyard_Brawl "Backyard Brawl"). In the huge upset win over [UCLA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UCLA "UCLA"), Butler had 13 points, while scoring 17 points against [Louisville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Louisville "University of Louisville") in the [Big East tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_East_Conference_Men's_Basketball_Player_of_the_Year "Big East Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year"). The Mountaineers eventually made it in the [NIT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Invitation_Tournament "National Invitation Tournament") Tournament, and all the way to the finals. In the finals win against [Clemson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clemson_University "Clemson University"), Butler had 20 points, as the Mountaineers were named NIT champions.

Butler was named to the [Big East](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_East_Conference "Big East Conference") all-freshman team, while leading the Mountaineers to an NIT Championship. Butler averaged 10.1 points per game, averaging 23.3 minutes per game off the bench, while also averaging 3.5 rebounds per game.

### Sophomore season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Da%27Sean_Butler&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Sophomore season")]

After the 2007 NIT Championship win, Mountaineers head coach [John Beilein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Beilein "John Beilein") announced he would be leaving [West Virginia University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Virginia_University "West Virginia University") to take the head coaching position at the [University of Michigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Michigan "University of Michigan"). Soon after, former head coach of [Kansas State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_State_University "Kansas State University")'s basketball team and West Virginia alumnus [Bob Huggins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Huggins "Bob Huggins") announced he accepted an offer to coach at West Virginia.

In the season-opening exhibition game against [Mountain State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mountain_State_University "Mountain State University"), Butler earned his first career start as the Mountaineers won 88–65. Butler scored 16 points and added 8 rebounds and three assists as he and fellow guard [Darris Nichols](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darris_Nichols "Darris Nichols") both went into double-digits in points. In the season-opener against [Arkansas-Monticello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Arkansas_at_Monticello "University of Arkansas at Monticello"), Butler scored 14 points while also grabbing a season-high 9 rebounds. In the 72–74 loss to [Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Tennessee "University of Tennessee"), Butler happened to score 16 points and grab 7 rebounds, while he scored 13 in the victories over New Mexico State and [Auburn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auburn_University "Auburn University"). Butler scored a season-high 18 points against [Duquesne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duquesne_University "Duquesne University"), while also grabbing 8 rebounds. He then scored 14 points against Maryland County, grabbing 9 rebounds, and [Radford University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radford_University "Radford University"), and then scored 10 against [Canisius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canisius_College "Canisius College").

In the 88–82 loss to [Oklahoma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Oklahoma "University of Oklahoma"), Butler scored 15 points and grabbed 5 rebounds. In the loss to [Notre Dame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Notre_Dame "University of Notre Dame"), Butler only scored 8 points but did grab 5 rebounds. Then in the victory over [Marquette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marquette_University "Marquette University"), Butler scored 13 points with 5 rebounds, but in the loss to [Louisville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Louisville "University of Louisville") he only scored 8 again. In the victory over [Syracuse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syracuse_University "Syracuse University"), Butler grabbed 6 rebounds to go along with his 13 points. Butler was key in the [St. John's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._John's_University_(New_York) "St. John's University (New York)") victory with 19 points and 9 rebounds. Butler recorded his first double-double of the season in the loss to [USF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_South_Florida "University of South Florida"), with 15 points and 12 rebounds. In the 66–64 victory over [Marshall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marshall_University "Marshall University"), Butler scored 18 points – including the game-winning shot in the lane with 6 seconds left.

Then in the 58–57 loss to No. 9 [Georgetown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgetown_University "Georgetown University"), Butler attempted to score the game-winning points again. However, his layup attempt was blocked by [Patrick Ewing Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_Ewing_Jr. "Patrick Ewing Jr.") The call was questionable however, as many believe it was actually a [goaltending](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goaltending "Goaltending") which would result in the points being rewarded and the Mountaineer-victory.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-1) However, Butler finished with 12 points and 4 rebounds. In an 81–63 victory over [Rutgers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rutgers "Rutgers"), Butler scored 12 points. He then followed that game with 15 points and 8 rebounds against [Seton Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seton_Hall "Seton Hall"). In the 78–56 loss to [Villanova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villanova_University "Villanova University"), Butler scored 10 points and grabbed 7 rebounds. In the 80–53 victory over [Providence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Providence_College "Providence College"), Butler scored 13 points and grabbed 4 rebounds.

In the 85–73 victory over [DePaul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DePaul_University "DePaul University") to gain the 20th win of the season, Butler scored 14 points and grabbed 13 rebounds for his second double-double of the season. In the 79–71 loss to the [Connecticut Huskies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connecticut_Huskies_men's_basketball "Connecticut Huskies men's basketball"), Butler scored 9 points and added 7 rebounds. In the home finale victory over the [Pittsburgh Panthers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh_Panthers "Pittsburgh Panthers"), 76–62, Butler scored 10 points and grabbed 6 rebounds. In the regular season finale, an 83–74 overtime victory over Providence, Butler scored 18 points, grabbed 10 rebounds, and dished 5 assists to finish the regular season. He finished the season with 12.5 points and 6.1 rebounds per game.

In the 58–53 victory over Providence to open the Big East tournament, Butler scored 17 points and added 9 rebounds. In the second round of the tourney, the Mountaineers upset #15-ranked Connecticut, 78–72. Butler contributed with 17 points and a team-high 9 rebounds. However, as the Mountaineers lost 55–72 in the semifinal matchup against the #8 [Georgetown Hoyas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgetown_Hoyas "Georgetown Hoyas"), Butler scored 16 points with 3 rebounds and assists.

In the first round of the [NCAA tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_NCAA_Men's_Division_I_Basketball_Tournament "2008 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament"), Butler scored 19 points with 7 rebounds as the No. 7-seed Mountaineers defeated the #10-seed [Arizona Wildcats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arizona_Wildcats "Arizona Wildcats"). In the second round, the Mountaineers upset the #2-seed [Duke Blue Devils](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duke_Blue_Devils "Duke Blue Devils") 73–67, with Butler scoring 8 points and grabbing 5 rebounds. Then, in the Sweet 16 loss in overtime to No. 3-seed [Xavier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xavier_Musketeers_men's_basketball "Xavier Musketeers men's basketball"), Butler scored 16 points and grabbed 7 rebounds.

Butler finished his sophomore season by averaging 12.9 points and 6.2 rebounds per game. During the Mountaineers Sweet 16 NCAA Tournament run, Butler averaged 14.3 points and 6.3 rebounds per game.

### Junior season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Da%27Sean_Butler&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Junior season")]

Butler began his junior season under returning head coach [Bob Huggins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Huggins "Bob Huggins") in the 98–78 exhibition win over [Mountain State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mountain_State_University "Mountain State University"). In the victory, Butler led the Mountaineers with 38 points and 11 rebounds. In the regular season opener against [Elon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elon_University "Elon University"), Butler scored 19 points and totaled 6 rebounds and steals. Against [Longwood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Longwood_University "Longwood University"), he then totaled 12 points and 4 rebounds. Opening the Las Vegas Invitational Tournament, the Mountaineers defeated [Delaware State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delaware_State "Delaware State"), with Butler scoring 12 points and grabbing 7 rebounds. He then scored 12 against [Iowa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iowa_Hawkeyes "Iowa Hawkeyes"), and before scoring 7 points with 9 boards in the loss to [Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kentucky_Wildcats "Kentucky Wildcats"). However, the Mountaineers then defeated [Mississippi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ole_Miss "Ole Miss"), with Butler scoring 22 points and grabbing 10 rebounds – his first double-double of the season. As the Mountaineers then beat [Cleveland State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland_State "Cleveland State"), Butler led the team with 18 points. In the 68–65 last-second loss to No. 22 [Davidson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Davidson_University "Davidson University") and [Stephen Curry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Curry "Stephen Curry") in [Madison Square Garden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madison_Square_Garden "Madison Square Garden"), Butler led the Mountaineers with 24 points and 14 rebounds – his second double-double in three games. Butler reached his 1,000 career points during the Miami University victory, in which he scored a career-high 28 points out of the team's 82–46 victory and also had 5 rebounds. Most Rebounds in his Career.

Butler then had 11 points against [Radford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radford_University "Radford University"), followed by 16 points and 6 rebounds in the 76–48 victory over #13 [Ohio State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ohio_State_Buckeyes "Ohio State Buckeyes"). In the 92–66 win over [Seton Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seton_Hall "Seton Hall"), Butler had 18 points, 9 rebounds and 5 assists. In the next loss to No. 5 [UConn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connecticut_Huskies "Connecticut Huskies"), 61–55, Butler scored 13 points and had 5 steals. As the Mountaineers then lost to No. 15 [Marquette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marquette_Golden_Eagles "Marquette Golden Eagles"), Butler scored 16 points and had 5 rebounds. Butler then had 17 points and 7 rebounds in the victory over [Marshall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marshall_University "Marshall University"). Against [South Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Florida_Bulls "South Florida Bulls"), Butler scored 27 points with 4 rebounds, and then he totaled 27 points and 8 rebounds in the win over #14 [Georgetown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgetown_Hoyas "Georgetown Hoyas"). In the following loss to No. 4 [Pittsburgh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh_Panthers "Pittsburgh Panthers"), Butler scored 21 points and had 6 rebounds. In the win over [St. John's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._John's_University_(New_York) "St. John's University (New York)"), Butler scored 21 points and had 7 rebounds. Butler recorded his fifth-consecutive 20-point game with 23 points against #7 [Louisville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisville_Cardinals "Louisville Cardinals") to go with 8 rebounds. Butler followed the Louisville loss with 23 points, 4 rebounds, 4 assists, and 4 steals against [Syracuse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syracuse_Orangemen "Syracuse Orangemen"). Butler's consecutive 20-point game streak ended at six games against [Providence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Providence_College "Providence College") with his 17 points and 9 rebounds in the 86–59 victory. In the [Backyard Brawl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Backyard_Brawl "Backyard Brawl") loss to No. 4 [Pittsburgh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh_Panthers "Pittsburgh Panthers"), Butler only scored 4 points in limited playing time due to foul trouble.

On February 13, the Mountaineers defeated #13 [Villanova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villanova_University "Villanova University") 93–72. In the victory, Butler scored a career-high 43 points; 24 points coming in the first-half. Butler's point total was the second-highest individual scoring performance in a Big East conference game since the 2002–03 season, only one-point shy of [Marcus Hatten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcus_Hatten "Marcus Hatten")'s 44 point performance in 2003.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-2) His 43 points were the third-most ever scored in the [WVU Coliseum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WVU_Coliseum "WVU Coliseum"), the most by a WVU player in conference play ever and the first 40-point performance since Lowes Moore in 1978.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-3) In the following 79–68 win over [Notre Dame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Notre_Dame_Fighting_Irish "Notre Dame Fighting Irish"), Butler had 19 points, 4 rebounds and 4 assists. He followed with 12 points and 4 assists in the win over [Rutgers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rutgers_Scarlet_Knights "Rutgers Scarlet Knights"). In the 65–61 loss to [Cincinnati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cincinnati_Bearcats "Cincinnati Bearcats"), Butler had 8 points and 4 assists. He then had 9 points and 12 rebounds in a win over [USF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Florida_Bulls "South Florida Bulls"). Butler then had a double-double in the win over [DePaul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DePaul_University "DePaul University") with 16 points and 10 rebounds. In the regular season finale against #6 [Louisville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisville_Cardinals "Louisville Cardinals"), Butler scored 10 points with 10 rebounds for a second-straight double-double. Following the 62–59 loss, he was named to the All-Big East second team.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-4)

In the second round of the Big East tournament against Notre Dame, Butler scored 20 points and grabbed 5 rebounds. In the quarterfinals' 74–60 win over #2 [Pittsburgh Panthers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh_Panthers "Pittsburgh Panthers"), Butler scored 16 points with 4 assists and 3 rebounds despite sitting out due to 4 personal fouls. In the semifinal round, a 74–69 loss to No. 20 [Syracuse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syracuse_Orangemen "Syracuse Orangemen"), Butler scored 21 points and had 6 rebounds. In the Big East tournament, Butler averaged 19 points and 4.6 rebounds. However, the Mountaineers were upset in the first round of the [NCAA tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NCAA_Men's_Division_I_Basketball_Championship "NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship") by [Dayton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Dayton "University of Dayton"), 68–60, with Butler scoring 12 points and grabbing 5 rebounds.

Butler finished his junior season with an average of 19.1 points per game and 5.9 rebounds per game. Butler had a season-high 43 points against Villanova and a season-high 14 rebounds against Davidson. Butler scored 20 or more points 12 times in the campaign.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-5)

### Senior season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Da%27Sean_Butler&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Senior season")]

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/41/Da%27Sean_Butler_2010_NCAA_West_Virginia_Elite_Eight.jpg/250px-Da%27Sean_Butler_2010_NCAA_West_Virginia_Elite_Eight.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Da'Sean_Butler_2010_NCAA_West_Virginia_Elite_Eight.jpg)

De'Sean Butler of West Virginia University lifts the East Region trophy after defeating Kentucky 73–66 in the 2010 NCAA men's basketball tournament.

Butler was invited to the 2009 USA Basketball Men's World University Games Team training camp prior to his senior season.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-6) Butler and the Top10-ranked Mountaineers opened up the season with a win over Loyola-Maryland, in which Butler recorded 26 points and 7 rebounds. In a later win over Portland, Butler scored 26 points with 6 rebounds. At the end of December, Butler hit a game-winning jumper to defeat Marquette, adding to his 17 total points.

After losing three games in early to mid-January, Butler and the Mountaineers bounced back with a win over #25 Ohio State and then a win over Louisville in which Butler scored 27 points. In a following win over St. John's, Butler scored 33 points, then he added 32 points in a triple overtime loss to No. 23 Pittsburgh. The Mountaineers ended their regular season with a 68–66 victory over #6 Villanova in which Butler had a double-double: 21 points and 10 rebounds.

In the Mountaineers' opening game of the Big East tournament, West Virginia defeated Cincinnati with help from Butler, who banked in the game-winning three-pointer with no time left to win 54–51. In the following 53–51 victory over [Notre Dame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Notre_Dame_Fighting_Irish "Notre Dame Fighting Irish") in the semifinals, Butler scored 24 points. In the championship game, Butler again led the Mountaineers to victory with the game-winning bucket over #22 Georgetown. The victory was the first ever Big East title for the Mountaineers.

Entering the NCAA Tournament as a two-seed, the Mountaineers handled Morgan State in the opening round. Butler scored 28 points and added 8 rebounds in the second round victory over Missouri. After defeating Washington in the Sweet 16, the Mountaineers upset the 1-seed and tourney favorite Kentucky Wildcats 73–66, to advance to the school's second Final Four appearance. Butler had 18 points in the Elite Eight victory, including finishing 4–8 from the 3-point line.

Butler and Duke's [Jon Scheyer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Scheyer "Jon Scheyer") were the only finalists in 2010's [Final Four](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Final_Four "Final Four") for the [Lowe's Senior CLASS Award for Men's Basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lowe's_Senior_CLASS_Award "Lowe's Senior CLASS Award"),[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-7) which on April 3, 2010, was awarded to Butler. Later that day, in the second half of the Final Four loss to the [Duke Blue Devils](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Duke_Blue_Devils_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team"), Butler injured his left knee. Butler tore his ACL, sprained his MCL and sustained two bone bruises.

Butler was one of 10 finalists for the 2010 [John R. Wooden Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_R._Wooden_Award "John R. Wooden Award").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-autogenerated4-8) It is given to the National Player of the Year in college basketball by The [Los Angeles Athletic Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Athletic_Club "Los Angeles Athletic Club").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-9)

## Professional career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Da%27Sean_Butler&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Professional career")]

### Austin Toros (2011)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Da%27Sean_Butler&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Austin Toros (2011)")]

After months of rehabilitation, Butler was selected by the Miami Heat 42nd overall in the 2010 NBA draft. Butler signed with the Heat on August 30, 2010.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-10) However, on October 25, Butler was waived by the Heat at the end of training camp.

On March 25, 2011, Butler signed a contract with the [San Antonio Spurs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Antonio_Spurs "San Antonio Spurs") and was assigned to the [Austin Toros](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austin_Spurs "Austin Spurs") of the [NBA Development League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_G_League "NBA G League").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-11)

### VEF Rīga (2011)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Da%27Sean_Butler&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: VEF Rīga (2011)")]

In November 2011 he joined [Latvian Basketball League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latvijas_Basketbola_l%C4%ABga "Latvijas Basketbola līga") club [VEF Rīga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BC_VEF_R%C4%ABga "BC VEF Rīga") during the [2011 NBA Lockout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_NBA_Lockout "2011 NBA Lockout").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-VEF-12)

### Return to Austin Toros (2011–2012)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Da%27Sean_Butler&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Return to Austin Toros (2011–2012)")]

Butler returned soon after to the San Antonio Spurs in time for the start of the 2011–2012 NBA season. He was officially waived by the Spurs on December 13, 2011.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-13)

He re-signed with the [Austin Toros](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austin_Spurs "Austin Spurs") during 2012, but was released towards the end of the season after requiring additional surgeries on the same knee.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-14)

### Okapi Aalstar (2013–2014)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Da%27Sean_Butler&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Okapi Aalstar (2013–2014)")]

On August 2, 2013, he signed with the Belgian team [Okapi Aalstar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Okapi_Aalstar "Okapi Aalstar") for the 2013–14 season.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-15) On April 30, 2014, Butler recorded a career-high 31 points, shooting 13-of-19 from the field, along with five rebounds, two assists and two steals in a 110–98 win over [Excelsior Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Excelsior_Brussels "Excelsior Brussels").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-16)

Butler won the [2013 Belgian Supercup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgian_Basketball_Supercup "Belgian Basketball Supercup") with Okapi Aalstar. In 48 games played during the 2013–14 season, he averaged 16.2 points, 4.2 rebounds, 1.2 assists and 1.2 steals per game. On June 15, 2014, Butler was named the Belgian League Forward of the Year and earned a spot in the All-Belgian League Second Team.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-17)

### Châlons Reims (2014–2015)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Da%27Sean_Butler&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Châlons Reims (2014–2015)")]

On June 22, 2014, he signed a one-year deal with the French team [Châlons Reims](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champagne_Ch%C3%A2lons_Reims_Basket "Champagne Châlons Reims Basket").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-18) On May 9, 2015, Butler recorded a season-high 24 points, shooting 9-of-13 from the field, along with four rebounds and three assists in an 85–75 win over [Pau-Orthez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%89lan_B%C3%A9arnais_Pau-Lacq-Orthez "Élan Béarnais Pau-Lacq-Orthez").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-19)

### ratiopharm Ulm (2015–2018)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Da%27Sean_Butler&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: ratiopharm Ulm (2015–2018)")]

On July 12, 2015, he signed with the German team [ratiopharm Ulm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ratiopharm_Ulm "Ratiopharm Ulm") for the 2014–15 season.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-20) On April 16, 2016, Butler recorded a season-high 27 points, shooting 7-of-10 from 3-point range, along with five rebounds, two assists and two steals in an 87–71 win over [Giessen 46ers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giessen_46ers "Giessen 46ers").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-21) Butler helped Ulm reach the [2016 BBL Finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_BBL_Playoffs "2016 BBL Playoffs"), where they eventually lost to [Brose Bamberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brose_Bamberg "Brose Bamberg").

On May 24, 2016, he re-signed with Ulm for the 2016–17 season.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-22) Butler helped Ulm reach the [2017 BBL Playoffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_BBL_Playoffs "2017 BBL Playoffs") as the first seed, but they eventually were eliminated by [EWE Baskets Oldenburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EWE_Baskets_Oldenburg "EWE Baskets Oldenburg") in the Semifinals.

On June 17, 2017, he signed a one-year contract extension with Ulm.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-23) In 23 BBL games played during the 2017–18 season, he averaged 10.3 points, 4.5 rebounds and 1.0 steals per game, shooting 39.6 percent from 3-point range.

### Hapoel Jerusalem (2018–2019)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Da%27Sean_Butler&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Hapoel Jerusalem (2018–2019)")]

On August 12, 2018, he signed a two-year deal with the Israeli team [Hapoel Jerusalem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hapoel_Jerusalem_B.C. "Hapoel Jerusalem B.C.").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-24) Butler won the [2019 Israeli State Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Israeli_Basketball_State_Cup "2018–19 Israeli Basketball State Cup") with Jerusalem.

### Hapoel Be'er Sheva (2019–2020)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Da%27Sean_Butler&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Hapoel Be'er Sheva (2019–2020)")]

On October 2, 2019, he signed with [Hapoel Be'er Sheva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hapoel_Be'er_Sheva_B.C. "Hapoel Be'er Sheva B.C.") for the 2019–20 season.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-25) On December 22, 2019, Butler recorded a season-high 25 points, including a three-pointer at the buzzer to give Be'er Sheva a 79–77 win over [Maccabi Ashdod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maccabi_Ashdod_B.C. "Maccabi Ashdod B.C.").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-26)

## Coaching career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Da%27Sean_Butler&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Coaching career")]

In February 2021, Butler joined [Wheeling University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wheeling_Cardinals "Wheeling Cardinals") as an assistant coach. He had been friends with the head coach Chris Richardson since he was 18 years old, and Richardson invited him to join his staff. In October 2021, Butler was hired as an assistant at the [College Park Skyhawks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_Park_Skyhawks "College Park Skyhawks") of the [NBA G League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_G_League "NBA G League").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-27)

In July 2023, Butler returned to his alma mater, [West Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Virginia_Mountaineers_men's_basketball "West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball"), as an assistant coach under [Josh Eilert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josh_Eilert "Josh Eilert").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-28)

In July 2024, Butler joined [Boston Celtics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston_Celtics "Boston Celtics") as a player enhancement coach under [Joe Mazzulla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla "Joe Mazzulla").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da'Sean_Butler#cite_note-29)
