**Jerome Adolphus Jordan** (born September 29, 1986) is a Jamaican former professional [basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball "Basketball") player. He played [college basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_basketball "College basketball") for the [University of Tulsa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tulsa_Golden_Hurricane_men's_basketball "Tulsa Golden Hurricane men's basketball") and represents the [Jamaica national team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamaica_national_basketball_team "Jamaica national basketball team") in international competition.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jerome_Jordan&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Jordan was born to parents Bryan and Faith Jordan in [Kingston, Jamaica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingston,_Jamaica "Kingston, Jamaica"), a city with just two hardwood courts, and it was not until age 16 that Jordan began playing basketball. Stephen Johnston, a former Jamaica national team captain, found a spot for Jordan at Redemption Christian Academy in [Troy, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troy,_New_York "Troy, New York"), which he attended with his sister, Jheanelle, while his parents stayed in Jamaica. However, after one semester, Bryan withdrew Jerome and Jheanelle from the school and they returned to Kingston.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-1)

After graduating from [Jamaica College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamaica_College "Jamaica College"),[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-2) Jordan enrolled at [Florida Air Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Air_Academy "Florida Air Academy") in [Melbourne, Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melbourne,_Florida "Melbourne, Florida"). However, he was ineligible to play in 2005–06 due to an academic transfer rule.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-3)

## College career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jerome_Jordan&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: College career")]

On April 26, 2006, Jordan signed a [National Letter of Intent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Letter_of_Intent "National Letter of Intent") to play college basketball for the [University of Tulsa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Tulsa "University of Tulsa").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-4)

In his freshman season at [Tulsa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tulsa_Golden_Hurricane_men's_basketball "Tulsa Golden Hurricane men's basketball") in 2006–07, Jordan played 23 games (10 starts) while averaging 2.7 points and 2.1 rebounds in 7.8 minutes per game.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-bio-5)

In his sophomore season, Jordan was named to the [Conference USA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conference_USA "Conference USA") All-Defensive team and All-Tournament team after a season where he finished second in the conference in [rebounds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebounds "Rebounds") and first in [field goal percentage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Field_goal_percentage "Field goal percentage") and [blocked shots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Block_(basketball) "Block (basketball)"). He also led Golden Hurricane to the [2008 CBI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_College_Basketball_Invitational "2008 College Basketball Invitational") championship and was named the tournament MVP. In 39 games (all starts), he averaged 10.5 points, 7.9 rebounds and 3.7 blocks per game.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-bio-5)

In his junior season, Jordan was named to the All-Conference USA first team after he earned Player of the Week honors four times.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-6) He was also named to the All-Defensive team for the second straight year after his 91 blocked shots gave him the number 1 and 2 positions on the school's single-season blocked shots list. In 36 games (35 starts), he averaged 13.8 points, 8.6 rebounds and 2.5 blocks per game.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-bio-5)

In his senior season, Jordan was named to the All-Conference USA second team and NABC Division I All-District 11 first team. In 35 games (all starts), he averaged 15.4 points, 9.1 rebounds and 2.4 blocks in 29.8 minutes per game.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-bio-5) He finished his career as the only player in Conference USA history to record at least 800 rebounds and 300 blocks, while setting the school and conference record for blocked shots with 333 blocks.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-bio-5)

## Professional career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jerome_Jordan&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Professional career")]

### 2010–11 season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jerome_Jordan&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2010–11 season")]

Jordan was selected with the 44th overall pick in the 2010 NBA draft by the [Milwaukee Bucks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milwaukee_Bucks "Milwaukee Bucks"). On July 8, 2010, his rights were traded to the [New York Knicks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Knicks "New York Knicks") in exchange for cash considerations.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-7) He joined the Knicks for the 2010 NBA Summer League. Later that year, he signed with [KK Hemofarm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KK_Vr%C5%A1ac "KK Vršac") of Serbia for the 2010–11 season.

### 2011–12 season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jerome_Jordan&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2011–12 season")]

On July 29, 2011, Jordan signed with [BC Krka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BC_Krka "BC Krka") of the [Premier A Slovenian Basketball League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premier_A_Slovenian_Basketball_League "Premier A Slovenian Basketball League").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-8) Following the conclusion of the [NBA lockout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_NBA_lockout "2011 NBA lockout"), he returned to the United States.

On December 15, 2011, Jordan signed with the New York Knicks.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-9) During the [2011–12 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011%E2%80%9312_NBA_season "2011–12 NBA season"), he was assigned multiple times to the [Erie BayHawks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erie_BayHawks_(2008%E2%80%932017) "Erie BayHawks (2008–2017)") of the [NBA Development League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Development_League "NBA Development League").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-10)

### 2012–13 season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jerome_Jordan&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 2012–13 season")]

On July 11, 2012, Jordan was traded, along with [Toney Douglas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toney_Douglas "Toney Douglas"), [Josh Harrellson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josh_Harrellson "Josh Harrellson") and two future second-round draft picks, to the [Houston Rockets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston_Rockets "Houston Rockets") in exchange for [Marcus Camby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcus_Camby "Marcus Camby").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-11) On July 18, 2012, he was waived by the Rockets.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-12) The next day, he joined the New York Knicks for the final two games of the 2012 NBA Summer League.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-13)

On September 29, 2012, Jordan signed with the [Memphis Grizzlies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memphis_Grizzlies "Memphis Grizzlies").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-14) However, he was later waived by the Grizzlies on October 27, 2012.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-15)

On December 18, 2012, Jordan was acquired by the [Reno Bighorns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reno_Bighorns "Reno Bighorns") of the NBA Development League.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-16) On February 4, 2013, he was named to the Futures All-Star roster for the 2013 NBA D-League All-Star Game.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-17)

On February 25, 2013, Jordan was traded to the [Los Angeles D-Fenders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_D-Fenders "Los Angeles D-Fenders").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-18) In April 2013, he joined the [Talk 'N Text Tropang Texters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk_'N_Text_Tropang_Texters "Talk 'N Text Tropang Texters") as an import for the 2013 Commissioner's Cup.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-19)

### 2013–14 season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jerome_Jordan&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 2013–14 season")]

In July 2013, Jordan joined the [Indiana Pacers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indiana_Pacers "Indiana Pacers") for the Orlando Summer League and the New York Knicks for the Las Vegas Summer League. On September 16, 2013, he signed with [Virtus Bologna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virtus_Pallacanestro_Bologna "Virtus Pallacanestro Bologna") of Italy for the 2013–14 season.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-20)

### 2014–15 season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jerome_Jordan&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: 2014–15 season")]

In July 2014, Jordan joined the [Los Angeles Lakers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Lakers "Los Angeles Lakers") for the [2014 NBA Summer League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_NBA_Summer_League "2014 NBA Summer League"). On September 11, 2014, he signed with the [Brooklyn Nets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn_Nets "Brooklyn Nets").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-21)

### 2015–16 season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jerome_Jordan&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: 2015–16 season")]

On October 11, 2015, Jordan signed with the [New Orleans Pelicans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans_Pelicans "New Orleans Pelicans").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-22) However, he was waived by the Pelicans on October 16 before appearing in a game with them.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-23) On December 15, he signed with [Jiangsu Monkey King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jiangsu_Monkey_King "Jiangsu Monkey King") of China for the [2015–16 CBA season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_CBA_season "2015–16 CBA season").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-24) After the end of the Chinese regular season, on February 20, he signed with [Baloncesto Sevilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baloncesto_Sevilla "Baloncesto Sevilla") of Spain for the rest of the [2015–16 ACB season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_ACB_season "2015–16 ACB season").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-25)

### 2016–17 season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jerome_Jordan&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: 2016–17 season")]

On October 31, 2016, Jordan signed with [Joventut Badalona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joventut_Badalona "Joventut Badalona") for the rest of the 2016–17 season.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-26)

### 2018–19 season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jerome_Jordan&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: 2018–19 season")]

On August 17, 2018, [Shaanxi Wolves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaanxi_Wolves "Shaanxi Wolves") of the [National Basketball League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Basketball_League_(China) "National Basketball League (China)") was reported to have signed Jordan.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-27) On September 30, he signed with [Cafés Candelas Breogán](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CB_Breog%C3%A1n "CB Breogán") of the [Liga ACB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liga_ACB "Liga ACB").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-28) On December 31, he signed with [Andorra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BC_Andorra "BC Andorra") of the [Liga ACB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liga_ACB "Liga ACB").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-29)

### 2019–20 season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jerome_Jordan&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: 2019–20 season")]

On January 3, 2020, he has signed with [Coosur Real Betis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Betis_Baloncesto "Real Betis Baloncesto") of the [Liga ACB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liga_ACB "Liga ACB"). [[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-30) Jordan averaged 7.5 points and 5.2 rebounds per game. Jordan parted ways with the team on June 2.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-31)

### 2020–21 season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jerome_Jordan&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: 2020–21 season")]

On August 1, 2020, Jordan signed with Al-Muharraq in Bahrain.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-32) On December 17, 2020, he has signed with [Real Betis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Betis_Baloncesto "Real Betis Baloncesto") of the [Liga ACB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liga_ACB "Liga ACB").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-33)

**Jerome Adolphus Jordan** (born September 29, 1986) is a Jamaican former professional [basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball "Basketball") player. He played [college basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_basketball "College basketball") for the [University of Tulsa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tulsa_Golden_Hurricane_men's_basketball "Tulsa Golden Hurricane men's basketball") and represents the [Jamaica national team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamaica_national_basketball_team "Jamaica national basketball team") in international competition.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jerome_Jordan&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Jordan was born to parents Bryan and Faith Jordan in [Kingston, Jamaica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingston,_Jamaica "Kingston, Jamaica"), a city with just two hardwood courts, and it was not until age 16 that Jordan began playing basketball. Stephen Johnston, a former Jamaica national team captain, found a spot for Jordan at Redemption Christian Academy in [Troy, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troy,_New_York "Troy, New York"), which he attended with his sister, Jheanelle, while his parents stayed in Jamaica. However, after one semester, Bryan withdrew Jerome and Jheanelle from the school and they returned to Kingston.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-1)

After graduating from [Jamaica College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamaica_College "Jamaica College"),[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-2) Jordan enrolled at [Florida Air Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Air_Academy "Florida Air Academy") in [Melbourne, Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melbourne,_Florida "Melbourne, Florida"). However, he was ineligible to play in 2005–06 due to an academic transfer rule.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-3)

## College career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jerome_Jordan&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: College career")]

On April 26, 2006, Jordan signed a [National Letter of Intent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Letter_of_Intent "National Letter of Intent") to play college basketball for the [University of Tulsa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Tulsa "University of Tulsa").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-4)

In his freshman season at [Tulsa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tulsa_Golden_Hurricane_men's_basketball "Tulsa Golden Hurricane men's basketball") in 2006–07, Jordan played 23 games (10 starts) while averaging 2.7 points and 2.1 rebounds in 7.8 minutes per game.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-bio-5)

In his sophomore season, Jordan was named to the [Conference USA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conference_USA "Conference USA") All-Defensive team and All-Tournament team after a season where he finished second in the conference in [rebounds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebounds "Rebounds") and first in [field goal percentage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Field_goal_percentage "Field goal percentage") and [blocked shots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Block_(basketball) "Block (basketball)"). He also led Golden Hurricane to the [2008 CBI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_College_Basketball_Invitational "2008 College Basketball Invitational") championship and was named the tournament MVP. In 39 games (all starts), he averaged 10.5 points, 7.9 rebounds and 3.7 blocks per game.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-bio-5)

In his junior season, Jordan was named to the All-Conference USA first team after he earned Player of the Week honors four times.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-6) He was also named to the All-Defensive team for the second straight year after his 91 blocked shots gave him the number 1 and 2 positions on the school's single-season blocked shots list. In 36 games (35 starts), he averaged 13.8 points, 8.6 rebounds and 2.5 blocks per game.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-bio-5)

In his senior season, Jordan was named to the All-Conference USA second team and NABC Division I All-District 11 first team. In 35 games (all starts), he averaged 15.4 points, 9.1 rebounds and 2.4 blocks in 29.8 minutes per game.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-bio-5) He finished his career as the only player in Conference USA history to record at least 800 rebounds and 300 blocks, while setting the school and conference record for blocked shots with 333 blocks.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-bio-5)

## Professional career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jerome_Jordan&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Professional career")]

### 2010–11 season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jerome_Jordan&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2010–11 season")]

Jordan was selected with the 44th overall pick in the 2010 NBA draft by the [Milwaukee Bucks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milwaukee_Bucks "Milwaukee Bucks"). On July 8, 2010, his rights were traded to the [New York Knicks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Knicks "New York Knicks") in exchange for cash considerations.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-7) He joined the Knicks for the 2010 NBA Summer League. Later that year, he signed with [KK Hemofarm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KK_Vr%C5%A1ac "KK Vršac") of Serbia for the 2010–11 season.

### 2011–12 season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jerome_Jordan&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2011–12 season")]

On July 29, 2011, Jordan signed with [BC Krka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BC_Krka "BC Krka") of the [Premier A Slovenian Basketball League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premier_A_Slovenian_Basketball_League "Premier A Slovenian Basketball League").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-8) Following the conclusion of the [NBA lockout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_NBA_lockout "2011 NBA lockout"), he returned to the United States.

On December 15, 2011, Jordan signed with the New York Knicks.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-9) During the [2011–12 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011%E2%80%9312_NBA_season "2011–12 NBA season"), he was assigned multiple times to the [Erie BayHawks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erie_BayHawks_(2008%E2%80%932017) "Erie BayHawks (2008–2017)") of the [NBA Development League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Development_League "NBA Development League").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-10)

### 2012–13 season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jerome_Jordan&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 2012–13 season")]

On July 11, 2012, Jordan was traded, along with [Toney Douglas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toney_Douglas "Toney Douglas"), [Josh Harrellson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josh_Harrellson "Josh Harrellson") and two future second-round draft picks, to the [Houston Rockets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston_Rockets "Houston Rockets") in exchange for [Marcus Camby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcus_Camby "Marcus Camby").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-11) On July 18, 2012, he was waived by the Rockets.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-12) The next day, he joined the New York Knicks for the final two games of the 2012 NBA Summer League.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-13)

On September 29, 2012, Jordan signed with the [Memphis Grizzlies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memphis_Grizzlies "Memphis Grizzlies").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-14) However, he was later waived by the Grizzlies on October 27, 2012.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-15)

On December 18, 2012, Jordan was acquired by the [Reno Bighorns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reno_Bighorns "Reno Bighorns") of the NBA Development League.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-16) On February 4, 2013, he was named to the Futures All-Star roster for the 2013 NBA D-League All-Star Game.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-17)

On February 25, 2013, Jordan was traded to the [Los Angeles D-Fenders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_D-Fenders "Los Angeles D-Fenders").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-18) In April 2013, he joined the [Talk 'N Text Tropang Texters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk_'N_Text_Tropang_Texters "Talk 'N Text Tropang Texters") as an import for the 2013 Commissioner's Cup.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-19)

### 2013–14 season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jerome_Jordan&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 2013–14 season")]

In July 2013, Jordan joined the [Indiana Pacers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indiana_Pacers "Indiana Pacers") for the Orlando Summer League and the New York Knicks for the Las Vegas Summer League. On September 16, 2013, he signed with [Virtus Bologna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virtus_Pallacanestro_Bologna "Virtus Pallacanestro Bologna") of Italy for the 2013–14 season.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-20)

### 2014–15 season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jerome_Jordan&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: 2014–15 season")]

In July 2014, Jordan joined the [Los Angeles Lakers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Lakers "Los Angeles Lakers") for the [2014 NBA Summer League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_NBA_Summer_League "2014 NBA Summer League"). On September 11, 2014, he signed with the [Brooklyn Nets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn_Nets "Brooklyn Nets").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-21)

### 2015–16 season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jerome_Jordan&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: 2015–16 season")]

On October 11, 2015, Jordan signed with the [New Orleans Pelicans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans_Pelicans "New Orleans Pelicans").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-22) However, he was waived by the Pelicans on October 16 before appearing in a game with them.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-23) On December 15, he signed with [Jiangsu Monkey King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jiangsu_Monkey_King "Jiangsu Monkey King") of China for the [2015–16 CBA season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_CBA_season "2015–16 CBA season").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-24) After the end of the Chinese regular season, on February 20, he signed with [Baloncesto Sevilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baloncesto_Sevilla "Baloncesto Sevilla") of Spain for the rest of the [2015–16 ACB season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_ACB_season "2015–16 ACB season").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-25)

### 2016–17 season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jerome_Jordan&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: 2016–17 season")]

On October 31, 2016, Jordan signed with [Joventut Badalona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joventut_Badalona "Joventut Badalona") for the rest of the 2016–17 season.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-26)

### 2018–19 season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jerome_Jordan&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: 2018–19 season")]

On August 17, 2018, [Shaanxi Wolves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaanxi_Wolves "Shaanxi Wolves") of the [National Basketball League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Basketball_League_(China) "National Basketball League (China)") was reported to have signed Jordan.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-27) On September 30, he signed with [Cafés Candelas Breogán](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CB_Breog%C3%A1n "CB Breogán") of the [Liga ACB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liga_ACB "Liga ACB").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-28) On December 31, he signed with [Andorra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BC_Andorra "BC Andorra") of the [Liga ACB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liga_ACB "Liga ACB").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-29)

### 2019–20 season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jerome_Jordan&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: 2019–20 season")]

On January 3, 2020, he has signed with [Coosur Real Betis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Betis_Baloncesto "Real Betis Baloncesto") of the [Liga ACB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liga_ACB "Liga ACB"). [[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-30) Jordan averaged 7.5 points and 5.2 rebounds per game. Jordan parted ways with the team on June 2.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-31)

### 2020–21 season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jerome_Jordan&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: 2020–21 season")]

On August 1, 2020, Jordan signed with Al-Muharraq in Bahrain.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-32) On December 17, 2020, he has signed with [Real Betis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Betis_Baloncesto "Real Betis Baloncesto") of the [Liga ACB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liga_ACB "Liga ACB").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Jordan#cite_note-33)
